title.zh: 卷19上 景穆十二王上
title.raw: 卷19上 景穆十二王上 Volume 19a: Emperor Jingmu Twelve Princes 1

sentences.zh: 陽平王 京兆王 濟陰王 汝陰王 樂浪王 廣平王

translations.literal: Prince of Yangping, Prince of Jingzhao, Prince of Jiyin, Prince of Ruyin, Prince of Leliang, Prince of Guangping
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Yangping, Jingzhao, Jiyin, Ruyin, Leliang, and Guangping

sentences.zh: 景穆皇帝十四男。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingmu had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu fathered fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 恭皇后生文成皇帝。

translations.literal: Empress Gong bore Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gong bore Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 袁椒房生陽平幽王新成。

translations.literal: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince You of Yangping, Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore Xincheng, Prince You of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 尉椒房生京兆康王子推、濟陰王小新成。

translations.literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Kang of Jingzhao, Tui, and the Prince of Jiyin, Xiao Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Tui, Prince Kang of Jingzhao, and Xiao Xincheng, Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 陽椒房生汝陰靈王天賜。

translations.literal: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Ling of Ruyin, Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore Tiansi, Prince Ling of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 樂良厲王萬壽、廣平殤王洛侯，母並闕。

translations.literal: Prince Li of Leliang, Wanshou, and Prince Shang of Guangping, Luohou—their mothers are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou, Prince Li of Leliang, and Luohou, Prince Shang of Guangping—both lack recorded mothers.

sentences.zh: 孟椒房生任城康王雲。

translations.literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Kang of Rencheng, Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Yun, Prince Kang of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 劉椒房生南安惠王楨、城陽康王長壽。

translations.literal: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Hui of Nan'an, Zhen, and Prince Kang of Chengyang, Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore Zhen, Prince Hui of Nan'an, and Changshou, Prince Kang of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 慕容椒房生章武敬王太洛。

translations.literal: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Jing of Zhangwu, Tailuo.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore Tailuo, Prince Jing of Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 尉椒房生樂陵康王胡兒。

translations.literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Kang of Leling, Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Hu'er, Prince Kang of Leling.

sentences.zh: 孟椒房生安定靖王休。

translations.literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince Jing of Anding, Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Xiu, Prince Jing of Anding.

sentences.zh: 趙王深早薨，無傳，母闕。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao, Shen, died young and left no biography; his mother is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Shen died young without a biography; his mother is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 魏舊太子後庭未有位號，高宗即位，恭宗宮人有子者，並號為椒房。

translations.literal: In old Wei the rear apartments of the crown prince had no formal ranks; when Gaozong took the throne, every Gongzong palace woman who had borne a son was styled of the Pepper Chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old Wei the crown prince's inner quarters had no formal titles; at Gaozong's accession every Gongzong consort who had borne a son was styled of the Pepper Chambers.

sentences.zh: 陽平王新成，太安三年封，拜征西大將軍。

translations.literal: Xincheng, Prince of Yangping, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tai'an and appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng, Prince of Yangping, received his fief in Tai'an year 3 and was made General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 後為內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Director of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰幽。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title You.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince You.

sentences.zh: 長子安壽，襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Anshou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Anshou succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜名頤。

translations.literal: Gaozu bestowed the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu granted him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 累遷懷朔鎮大將，都督三道諸軍事，北討。

translations.literal: By successive promotion he became Grand General of Huaiyuan Garrison, commander of military affairs on all three routes, and marched north to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand General of Huaiyuan Garrison and commander of the three northern routes on campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔徵赴京，勗以戰伐之事。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and urged him on matters of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and exhorted on the conduct of war.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當仰仗廟算，使呼韓同渭橋之禮。

translations.literal: He replied: "One must rely on the temple's plans and make the Khan submit as at Weiqiao Bridge."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "We should trust the court's strategy and bring the khan to homage as at Weiqiao Bridge."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘆曰：「壯哉王言！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "How bold the prince's words!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed. "What bold words from the prince!"

sentences.zh: 朕所望也。

translations.literal: That is what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: That is exactly what I hope for."

sentences.zh: 」未發，遭母憂，詔遣侍臣以金革敦喻。

translations.literal: Before he set out he suffered his mother's death; an edict sent palace attendants to urge him with the metal-and-leather exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched he entered mourning for his mother; attendants were sent to urge him back to duty under the metal-and-leather rule.

sentences.zh: 既殯而發，與陸叡集三道諸將議軍途所詣。

translations.literal: After the burial he set out and with Lu Rui gathered the generals of the three routes to decide the army's course.
translations.idiomatic: Once the burial was done he took the field; with Lu Rui he convened the three-route commanders to fix the line of march.

sentences.zh: 於是中道出黑山，東道趨士盧河，西道向侯延河。

translations.literal: Thereupon the center route went out by Black Mountain, the east route toward the Shilu River, and the west route toward the Houyan River.
translations.idiomatic: The center column crossed Black Mountain, the east column pressed the Shilu River, and the west column the Houyan River.

sentences.zh: 軍過大磧，大破蠕蠕。

translations.literal: The army crossed the Great Marsh and routed the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Great Marsh they shattered the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 頤入朝，詔曰：「王之前言，果不虛也。

translations.literal: When Yi came to court, an edict said: "The prince's earlier words were not empty."
translations.idiomatic: On Yi's return an edict read, "Your earlier boast was no empty boast."

sentences.zh: 」後除朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed inspector of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 及恒州刺史穆泰謀反遣使推頤為主。

translations.literal: When Mu Tai, inspector of Hengzhou, plotted rebellion he sent envoys urging Yi to be their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Hengzhou inspector Mu Tai rebelled he sent messengers offering Yi the leadership.

sentences.zh: 頤密以狀聞，泰等伏誅，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Yi secretly reported the matter; Tai and the rest were executed, and the emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported in secret; Tai and his party were put to death, and the emperor richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明元年，薨於青州刺史，[2]諡曰莊王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming of Emperor Shizong he died as inspector of Qingzhou,[2] posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizong's Jingming year 1 he died in office at Qingzhou,[2] and was posthumously titled Prince Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫宗胤，肅宗時，坐殺叔父賜死，爵除。

translations.literal: The line passed to his grandson Zongyin; in Suzong's time, for killing his uncle he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his grandson Zongyin; under Suzong he was executed for murdering his uncle and the fief was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 頤弟衍，字安樂，賜爵廣陵侯。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Yan, styled Anle, was granted the rank Marquis of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's brother Yan, courtesy name Anle, was made Marquis of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 位梁州刺史，表請假王，以崇威重。

translations.literal: As inspector of Liangzhou he memorialized asking to be made acting king to lend weight to his authority.
translations.idiomatic: As Liangzhou inspector he asked to be made acting king so his authority would carry more weight.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可謂無厭求也，所請不合。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This may be called insatiable asking; the request does not accord."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, "This is sheer greed—the request is denied."

sentences.zh: 」轉徐州刺史，至州病重，帝敕徐成伯乘傳療。

translations.literal: Transferred to inspector of Xuzhou, he fell gravely ill on reaching the province; the emperor ordered Xu Chengbai to ride post-haste to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Xuzhou, he fell gravely ill on arrival; the emperor sent Xu Chengbai by express relay to heal him.

sentences.zh: 疾差，成伯還，帝曰「卿定名醫」，賚絹三千匹。

translations.literal: When the illness eased and Chengbai returned, the emperor said, "You are a true famous physician," and rewarded him with three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan recovered and Chengbai returned, the emperor said, "You are a physician of name indeed," and gave him three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 成伯辭，請受一千。

translations.literal: Chengbai declined and asked to receive only one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbai refused and asked for only one thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「詩云『人之云亡，邦國殄瘁。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Odes say, 'When men of worth perish, the state is laid waste.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Odes say, 'When worthy men are lost, the state withers.'"

sentences.zh: 』以是而言，豈惟三千匹乎？

translations.literal: By that reckoning, is it only three thousand bolts?"
translations.idiomatic: "By that measure, would three thousand bolts be enough?"

sentences.zh: 」其為帝所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight the emperor gave him.
translations.idiomatic: So highly did the emperor value him.

sentences.zh: 後所生母雷氏卒，表請解州。

translations.literal: Later, when his birth mother Lady Lei died, he memorialized asking to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his birth mother Lady Lei died, he asked to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先君餘尊之所厭，禮之明文，季末陵遲，斯典或廢。

translations.literal: An edict said: "What the former prince's residual honor abhors is plain in the rites; in the late age rites decayed and this canon was sometimes abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "The rites plainly say what a former prince's residual honor forbids; in late days that canon was often abandoned."

sentences.zh: 侯既親王之子，宜從餘尊之義，便可大功。

translations.literal: As the marquis is a king's son, he should follow the residual-honor rule and may observe only the greater mourning."
translations.idiomatic: "As a king's son you should follow residual honor and observe only the greater mourning period."

sentences.zh: 」後卒於雍州刺史，諡曰康侯。

translations.literal: Later he died as inspector of Yongzhou, posthumous title Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as Yongzhou inspector and was posthumously titled Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 衍性清慎，所在廉潔，又不營產業，歷牧四州，皆有稱績，亡日無斂屍具。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature cautious and pure; wherever he served he was incorrupt, kept no estates, and through four provincial governorships won praise—yet on the day he died there was not even a shroud for his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was sober and careful, incorrupt in every post, and built no estates; through four governorships he won praise, yet the day he died his household could not furnish a burial shroud.

sentences.zh: 子暢。

translations.literal: His son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chang.

sentences.zh: 暢弟融，字叔。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Rong, styled Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Rong, courtesy name Shu.

sentences.zh: 融貌甚短陋，驍武過人。

translations.literal: Rong's appearance was very short and ugly, yet his martial valor surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was remarkably short and plain of face, yet fiercer in arms than most men.

sentences.zh: 莊帝謀殺尒朱榮，以融為直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang plotted to kill Erzhu Rong, Rong was made Direct-Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang plotted Erzhu Rong's death, Rong was made Direct-Gate General.

sentences.zh: 及尒朱兆入洛，融逃人間。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Rong hid among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, Rong vanished into the crowd.

sentences.zh: 衍弟欽，字思若。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Qin, styled Siruo.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's brother Qin, courtesy name Siruo.

sentences.zh: 位中書監、尚書右僕射、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He held the posts Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Pillar of State, third rank.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Pillar of State of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 欽色尤黑，故時人號為黑面僕射。

translations.literal: Qin's complexion was especially dark, so people of the time called him the Black-Faced Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's complexion was unusually dark, and men called him the Black-Faced Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 欽淫從兄麗妻崔氏，為御史中尉封回劾奏，遇赦免。

translations.literal: Qin debauched the wife of his cousin Li, née Cui; Censor-in-Chief Feng Hui impeached him, but he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin seduced his cousin Li's wife, née Cui; Censor-in-Chief Feng Hui impeached him, but an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 尋除司州牧。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 欽少好學，早有令譽，時人語曰：「皇宗略略，壽安、思若。

translations.literal: Qin from youth loved learning and early won a fine reputation; people said: "Among the imperial clan, broadly speaking—Shou'an and Siruo."
translations.idiomatic: Qin loved books from youth and won early fame; people said, "Among the royal house, take Shou'an and Siruo."

sentences.zh: 」及晚年貴重，不能有所匡益，識者輕之。

translations.literal: In later years, though he grew weighty in rank, he could not correct or aid the state; men of judgment looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later eminence he offered the court little counsel, and discerning men held him cheap.

sentences.zh: 欽曾託青州人高僧壽為子求師，師至，未幾逃去。

translations.literal: Qin once asked the Qingzhou man Gaosengshou to find a tutor for his son; when the tutor arrived he fled after only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once asked Gaosengshou of Qingzhou to find his son a tutor; the man came, then fled within days.

sentences.zh: 欽以讓僧壽。

translations.literal: Qin reproached Gaosengshou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin blamed Gaosengshou.

sentences.zh: 僧壽性滑稽，反謂欽曰：「凡人絕粒，七日乃死，始經五朝，便爾逃遁，去食就信，實有所闕。

translations.literal: Gaosengshou, by nature a jester, turned and said to Qin: "Ordinary men who stop eating die in seven days; this one lasted only five mornings before running off—he left food for faith, and plainly lacked something."
translations.idiomatic: Gaosengshou, a born jester, shot back: "A man who stops eating dies in seven days; yours lasted five mornings and bolted—he chose faith over food, and plainly lacked something."

sentences.zh: 」欽乃大慚，於是待客稍厚。

translations.literal: Qin was deeply ashamed and from then treated guests somewhat better.
translations.idiomatic: Qin flushed with shame and afterward treated guests a little more generously.

sentences.zh: 後除司空公，封鉅平縣公。

translations.literal: Later he was made Duke of Works and enfeoffed Duke of Juping county.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Duke of Works and enfeoffed Duke of Juping county.

sentences.zh: 於河陰遇害，贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉公。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously given the yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin and posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 子子孝，字季業。

translations.literal: His son Zixiao, styled Jiye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixiao, courtesy name Jiye.

sentences.zh: 早有令譽，年八歲，司徒崔光見而異之曰：「後生領袖，必此人也。」

translations.literal: Early he had a fine reputation; at eight years Minister of State Cui Guang saw him and marveled, saying, "The coming leader of the younger generation will surely be this boy."
translations.idiomatic: He won early fame; at eight Minister of State Cui Guang marveled at him and said, "The next generation's leader will be this boy."

sentences.zh: 子太興，襲。

translations.literal: His son Taixing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taixing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 拜長安鎮都大將，以黷貨，削除官爵。

translations.literal: Made Grand General of Chang'an Garrison, for corruption he was stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand General of Chang'an Garrison he was removed from office and title for corruption.

sentences.zh: 後除祕書監，還復前爵，拜統萬鎮將，改封西河。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former title, made commander of Tongwan Garrison, and re-enfeoffed in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He was later Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former rank, made commander of Tongwan Garrison, and re-enfeoffed in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 後改鎮為夏州，仍以太興為刺史。

translations.literal: Later the garrison was changed to Xiazhou, and Taixing remained inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the post was renamed Xiazhou, Taixing stayed on as inspector.

sentences.zh: 除守衞尉卿。

translations.literal: He was made Acting Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 初，太興遇患，請諸沙門行道，所有資財，一時布施，乞求病愈，名曰「散生齋」。

translations.literal: At first, when Taixing fell ill, he asked Buddhist monks to perform rites and at once gave away all his goods, begging recovery—the rite was called the "Life-Scattering Fast."
translations.idiomatic: When Taixing first fell ill he had monks perform rites and gave away his entire fortune to beg a cure—a feast he called the Life-Scattering Fast.

sentences.zh: 及齋後，僧皆四散，有一沙門方云乞齋餘食。

translations.literal: After the fast the monks all dispersed; one monk was just asking for leftover food from the fast.
translations.idiomatic: When the fast ended the monks scattered; one lingered, asking for leftovers.

sentences.zh: 太興戲之曰：「齋食既盡，唯有酒肉。

translations.literal: Taixing jested: "The fast food is gone; only wine and meat remain."
translations.idiomatic: Taixing teased him: "The fast fare is spent—only wine and meat are left."

sentences.zh: 」沙門曰：「亦能食之。

translations.literal: The monk said: "I can eat those too."
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "I can eat those as well."

sentences.zh: 」因出酒一斗，羊脚一隻，食盡猶言不飽。

translations.literal: So he brought out a dou of wine and a sheep's leg; the monk ate all and still said he was not full.
translations.idiomatic: They brought a dou of wine and a sheep's leg; he ate everything and still claimed hunger.

sentences.zh: 及辭出後，酒肉俱在，出門追之，無所見。

translations.literal: After he left, wine and meat were still there; going out the gate to pursue him, nothing was seen.
translations.idiomatic: When he had gone, the wine and meat remained untouched; men chased him beyond the gate but found no one.

sentences.zh: 太興遂佛前乞願，向者之師當非俗人，若此病得差，即捨王爵入道。

translations.literal: Taixing then prayed before the Buddha that the visitor must be no ordinary man; if this illness were cured he would abandon his princely title and enter the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing prayed before the Buddha that such a visitor could not be ordinary; if he recovered he would surrender his title and take orders.

sentences.zh: 未幾便愈，遂請為沙門，表十餘上，乃見許。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered, then asked to become a monk; he memorialized more than ten times before permission came.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recovered, petitioned repeatedly to become a monk, and after a dozen memorials was allowed.

sentences.zh: 時高祖南討在軍，詔皇太子於四月八日為之下髮，施帛二千匹。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was campaigning south in the field; an edict ordered the crown prince on the eighth day of the fourth month to tonsure him and grant two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then campaigning in the south; the crown prince was ordered to tonsure him on the eighth day of the fourth month and grant two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 既為沙門，更名僧懿，居嵩山。

translations.literal: Having become a monk, he took the name Sengyi and lived on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: As a monk he took the name Sengyi and dwelt on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 太和二十二年終。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 22.

sentences.zh: 子昴，字伯暉，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ang, styled Bohui, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang, courtesy name Bohui, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子悰，字魏慶，襲。

translations.literal: His son Cong, styled Weiqing, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong, courtesy name Weiqing, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，累遷太尉、錄尚書事、司州牧、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, governor of Sizhou, and inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaojing he became Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, governor of Sizhou, and inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨於州，贈假黃鉞、太傅、司徒公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumously given the yellow battle-axe, Grand Tutor, and Duke of the State, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the yellow battle-axe, Grand Tutor, and Duke of the State with the title Wen.

sentences.zh: [3]悰寬和有度量，美容貌，風望儼然，得喪之間，不見於色。

translations.literal: [3]Cong was generous and measured, handsome of face, and carried himself with grave dignity; between gain and loss his color did not change.
translations.idiomatic: [3]Cong was open-handed and even-tempered, handsome, and grave in bearing; fortune and misfortune alike left his face unchanged.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，不營產業，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal and kept no estates; on the day he died the house held no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and built no estates; the day he died his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 昴弟仲景，性嚴峭。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Zhongjing was by nature stern and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's brother Zhongjing was severe by nature.

sentences.zh: 莊帝時，兼御史中尉，京師肅然。

translations.literal: In Emperor Zhuang's time he concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief, and the capital grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuang he also served as Censor-in-Chief, and the capital grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 每向臺，恒駕赤牛，時人號「赤牛中尉」。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to the bureau he always drove a red ox, so people called him the Red-Ox Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He always drove a red ox to the bureau, and men called him the Red-Ox Censor.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，為河南尹，奉法無私。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was Intendant of Henan and enforced the law without private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was Intendant of Henan and enforced the law without favor.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書樊子鵠部下縱橫，又為盜竊，仲景密加收捕，悉獲之，咸即行決，於是豪貴寒心。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Personnel Fan Zihe's subordinates ran rampant and also committed theft; Zhongjing secretly arrested and seized them all and at once executed them, so the powerful grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Fan Zihe's men were running riot and stealing; Zhongjing seized them in secret, executed them on the spot, and the great families trembled.

sentences.zh: 出帝將西行，授仲景中軍大都督，留京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu was about to go west, Zhongjing was made Grand Commander of the Central Army and left in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Chu prepared to move west, Zhongjing was made Grand Commander of the Central Army and left to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王欲至洛陽，仲景遂棄妻子而遁。

translations.literal: King Xianwu of Qi wished to reach Luoyang; Zhongjing then abandoned wife and children and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xianwu of Qi marched on Luoyang, Zhongjing deserted wife and children and fled.

sentences.zh: 子沖，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 無子，國絕。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons, and the fief died out.

sentences.zh: 太興弟遙，字太原。

translations.literal: Taixing's younger brother Yao, styled Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing's younger brother Yao, courtesy name Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 有器望，以左衞將軍從高祖南征，賜爵饒陽男。

translations.literal: He had ability and standing; as Left Guard General he followed Gaozu on the southern campaign and was granted the rank Baron of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and respected, he followed Gaozu south as Left Guard General and was made Baron of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，遭所生母憂，表請解任，詔以餘尊所厭，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he suffered his birth mother's death and memorialized asking to leave office; an edict said the residual-honor rule forbade it and did not allow.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he mourned his birth mother and asked to resign; an edict cited residual honor and refused.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，累遷左光祿大夫，仍領護軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he rose by stages to Left Grand Master of the Palace and still headed the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he rose to Left Grand Master of the Palace while still commanding the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 遷冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: [4]遙以諸胡先無籍貫，姦良莫辨，悉令造籍。

translations.literal: [4]Yao, because the various Hu previously had no household registers and good and bad could not be distinguished, ordered them all to compile registers.
translations.idiomatic: [4]Because the frontier Hu had no household registers and criminals could not be told from honest men, Yao ordered every household registered.

sentences.zh: 又以諸胡設籍；

translations.literal: He also had the various Hu registered;
translations.idiomatic: He also registered the Hu clans;

sentences.zh: 當欲稅之，以充軍用。

translations.literal: he meant to tax them to fill military needs.
translations.idiomatic: he meant to tax them to fund the army.

sentences.zh: 胡人不願，乃共構遙，云取納金馬。

translations.literal: The Hu were unwilling and together framed Yao, saying he took bribes of gold and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu resisted and jointly accused Yao of taking gold and horses in bribes.

sentences.zh: 御史按驗，事與胡同，遙坐除名。

translations.literal: The censorate investigated; the facts agreed with the Hu's charge, and Yao was dismissed and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate investigated, found the charges matched, and Yao was removed and struck from office.

sentences.zh: 遙陳枉不已，敕有司重究，乃披雪。

translations.literal: Yao pleaded his innocence without cease; an edict ordered the offices to reinvestigate, and he was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Yao protested his innocence until an edict ordered a new inquiry and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 遷右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Right Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Right Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 時冀州沙門法慶既為祅幻，遂說勃海人李歸伯，歸伯合家從之，招率鄉人，推法慶為主。

translations.literal: At that time in Jizhou the monk Fazheng had turned to heterodox sorcery and persuaded the Bohai man Li Guibo; Guibo's whole household followed him, he gathered fellow villagers, and they made Fazheng their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In Jizhou the monk Fazheng had taken up demonic sorcery and won over Li Guibo of Bohai; Guibo's household and neighbors followed, and they set Fazheng at their head.

sentences.zh: 法慶以歸伯為十住菩薩、平魔軍司、定漢王，自號「大乘」。

translations.literal: Fazheng made Guibo Ten-Abiding Bodhisattva, Pacifying-Demons Army Marshal, and King Who Settles Han; he styled himself "Mahayana."
translations.idiomatic: Fazheng named Guibo Ten-Abiding Bodhisattva, Marshal of the Army That Pacifies Demons, and King Who Settles the Han, while he called himself Mahayana.

sentences.zh: 殺一人者為一住菩薩，殺十人為十住菩薩。

translations.literal: Whoever killed one man was a One-Abiding Bodhisattva; whoever killed ten was a Ten-Abiding Bodhisattva.
translations.idiomatic: One murder made a One-Abiding Bodhisattva; ten murders made a Ten-Abiding Bodhisattva.

sentences.zh: 又合狂藥，令人服之，父子兄弟不相知識，唯以殺害為事。

translations.literal: They also mixed mad drugs; whoever took them no longer knew father, brother, or son, and knew only killing.
translations.idiomatic: They brewed frenzy-drugs; under their spell kin no longer recognized one another and knew only slaughter.

sentences.zh: 於是聚眾殺阜城令，破勃海郡，殺害吏人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered a mob, killed the magistrate of Fucheng, stormed Bohai commandery, and slaughtered officials and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: They raised a mob, killed Fucheng's magistrate, stormed Bohai commandery, and butchered officials and clerks.

sentences.zh: 刺史蕭寶夤遣兼長史崔伯驎討之，敗於煮棗城，伯驎戰沒。

translations.literal: Inspector Xiao Baoyin sent Acting Chief Clerk Cui Bolin to attack them; he was defeated at Zhuzao city and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xiao Baoyin sent Acting Chief Clerk Cui Bolin against them; Bolin was beaten at Zhuzao city and killed.

sentences.zh: 凶眾遂盛，所在屠滅寺舍，斬戮僧尼，焚燒經像，云新佛出世，除去舊魔。

translations.literal: The rebels then swelled; wherever they went they massacred monasteries, cut down monks and nuns, burned sutras and images, saying a new Buddha had come to clear away the old demons.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swelled, razing monasteries, slaughtering monks and nuns, and burning sutras and icons, proclaiming a new Buddha come to sweep away the old demons.

sentences.zh: 詔以遙為使持節、都督北征諸軍事，帥步騎十萬以討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Yao bearer of the staff, commander of all armies on the northern expedition, and he led a hundred thousand foot and horse to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was commissioned bearer of the staff, commander of the northern expedition, and led a hundred thousand foot and horse against them.

sentences.zh: 法慶相率攻遙，遙並擊破之。

translations.literal: Fazheng together attacked Yao; Yao defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fazheng massed to strike Yao; Yao broke every attack.

sentences.zh: 遙遣輔國將軍張虯等率騎追掩，討破，擒法慶并其妻尼惠暉等，斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Yao sent the Assistant General Who Supports the State Zhang Niu and others with cavalry in pursuit; they routed the band, captured Fazheng with his wife the nun Huihui and the rest, beheaded them, and sent the heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yao sent Assistant General Zhang Niu and others in pursuit; they crushed the sect, seized Fazheng with his wife the nun Huihui, beheaded them, and sent the heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後擒歸伯，戮於都巿。

translations.literal: Later Guibo was captured and executed at the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: Guibo was later taken and executed in the capital market.

sentences.zh: 初，遙大功昆弟，皆是恭宗之孫，至肅宗而本服絕，故除遙等屬籍。

translations.literal: At first Yao and his brothers in greater mourning were all grandsons of Gongzong; by Suzong's time the original mourning tie was exhausted, so Yao and the rest were struck from the imperial registry.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and his brothers had worn greater mourning for Gongzong; by Suzong's reign that original tie was spent, and they were removed from the imperial registry.

sentences.zh: 遙表曰：「竊聞聖人所以南面而聽天下，其不可得變革者，則親也，尊也。

translations.literal: Yao memorialized: "I have heard that the sage faces south to hear all under Heaven; what cannot be altered are kinship and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yao memorialized: "I hear that the sage faces south to rule the realm; what cannot be changed are kinship and honor."

sentences.zh: 四世而緦服窮，五世而袒免，六世而親屬竭矣。

translations.literal: At the fourth generation the finest mourning ends; at the fifth the bared shoulder; at the sixth, kinship is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth generation the finest mourning ends; at the fifth the shoulder is bared; at the sixth, kinship is spent."

sentences.zh: 去茲以往，猶繫之以姓而弗別，綴之以食而弗殊。

translations.literal: Beyond that, men are still bound by surname without division, and joined by food without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, men still share a surname without being severed, and share a meal without being set apart."

sentences.zh: 又律云議親者，非唯當世之屬親，歷謂先帝之五世。

translations.literal: The law also says that in deliberating kin, one counts not only the present generation's kin but the former emperor's five generations.
translations.idiomatic: The law also says that in weighing kin one counts not only the living generation but the former emperor's five generations."

sentences.zh: 謹尋斯旨，將以廣帝宗，重盤石。

translations.literal: Carefully tracing this intent, it is meant to broaden the imperial clan and weight the foundation stones.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing that intent, it was meant to widen the imperial house and steady the realm's pillars."

sentences.zh: 先皇所以變茲事條，為此別制者，太和之季，方有意於吳蜀，經始之費，慮深在初，割減之起，暫出當時也。

translations.literal: The reason the late emperor altered this statute and made this separate rule was that in the Taihe years he had his mind on Wu and Shu; the costs of beginning were feared at the start, and the cuts arose only for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor changed this statute only because in the Taihe years his mind was on Wu and Shu; startup costs frightened him at the outset, and the cuts were a temporary measure."

sentences.zh: 且臨淮王提，分屬籍之始，高祖賜帛三千匹，所以重分離；

translations.literal: Moreover Prince Ti of Huaiyang, at the very start of being struck from the registry, received three thousand bolts of silk from Gaozu to mark the weight of separation;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ti of Huaiyang was first struck from the rolls, Gaozu gave him three thousand bolts of silk to mark how heavy the parting was;

sentences.zh: 樂良王長命，亦賜縑二千匹，所以存慈眷。

translations.literal: Prince Changming of Leliang also received two thousand bolts of silk to preserve affectionate regard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changming of Leliang received two thousand bolts to preserve affectionate regard.

sentences.zh: 此皆先朝殷勤克念，不得已而然者也。

translations.literal: These were all the former court's earnest, compelled thought—things done because there was no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Those were all the former court's reluctant concessions—things done because there was no choice."

sentences.zh: 古人有言，百足之蟲至死不僵者，以其輔己者眾。

translations.literal: The ancients said that even a centipede does not stiffen until death because those who aid it are many.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said a centipede does not stiffen until death because so many legs still support it."

sentences.zh: 臣誠不欲妄親太階，苟求潤屋，但傷大宗一分，則天子屬籍不過十數人而已。

translations.literal: Your servant truly does not wish rashly to climb the great stairs or seek to fatten his house, but it wounds me that the great house loses a share and the Son of Heaven's registry holds barely a dozen names.
translations.idiomatic: I do not seek to climb high or swell my household, but it grieves me that the great house loses a branch and the Son of Heaven's registry holds barely a dozen names."

sentences.zh: 在漢，諸王之子不限多少，皆列土而封，謂之曰侯，至于魏晉，莫不廣胙河山，稱之曰公者，蓋惡其大宗之不固，骨肉之恩疏矣。

translations.literal: Under Han, kings' sons were not limited in number—all received fiefs as marquises; by Wei and Jin none failed to broaden enfeoffments across rivers and mountains and style them dukes, because they hated that the great house was not firm and the bone-and-flesh bond had grown thin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han every king's son, however many, received a fief as marquis; under Wei and Jin enfeoffments sprawled across the land as dukes, for they feared a weak great house and thinning kinship."

sentences.zh: 臣去皇上，雖是五世之遠，於先帝便是天子之孫，高祖所以國秩祿賦復給衣食，后族唯給其賦不與衣食者，欲以別外內限異同也。

translations.literal: Your servant, though five generations from the present sovereign, to the late emperor was still the Son of Heaven's grandson; Gaozu therefore restored state rank, salary, and grain, again granting food and clothing—while the empress's kin received grain but not clothing, wishing to separate inner from outer and mark the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Though I stand five generations from Your Majesty, to the late emperor I was still the Son of Heaven's grandson; Gaozu restored rank, salary, and grain and again granted food and clothing—whereas the empress's kin received grain but not clothing, to mark inner from outer."

sentences.zh: 今諸廟之感，在心未忘；

translations.literal: Now the feeling owed the ancestral temples is not yet forgotten in the heart;
translations.idiomatic: The debt owed the ancestral temples is not yet forgotten;

sentences.zh: 行道之悲，倏然已及。

translations.literal: the grief of walking the rites has suddenly already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: the grief of walking the mourning rites has suddenly come upon us."

sentences.zh: 其諸封者，身亡之日，三年服終，然後改奪。

translations.literal: For all who hold fiefs, on the day they die, when the three-year mourning ends, only then should titles be altered and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: For every enfeoffed prince, only when three years' mourning after his death is finished should titles be altered or withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 今朝廷猶在遏密之中，便議此事，實用未安。

translations.literal: Now the court is still in the stifled-grief period, yet this matter is already debated—truly it is not yet fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The court is still in stifled grief, yet this is already debated—truly the time is not right."

sentences.zh: 」詔付尚書博議以聞。

translations.literal: An edict sent the memorial to the Masters of Writing for broad deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the memorial to the Masters of Writing for broad deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書令任城王澄、尚書左僕射元暉奏同遙表。

translations.literal: Minister of State Prince Cheng of Rencheng and Left Vice Minister Yuan Hui memorialized agreement with Yao's table.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of State Prince Cheng of Rencheng and Left Vice Minister Yuan Hui memorialized in agreement with Yao.

sentences.zh: 靈太后不從。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling would not agree.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰宣公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Duke Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Duke Xuan.

sentences.zh: 遙弟恒，字景安，粗涉書史。

translations.literal: Yao's younger brother Heng, styled Jing'an, had rough knowledge of books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's brother Heng, courtesy name Jing'an, had a rough schooling in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 恒以春秋之義，為名不以山川，表求改名芝。

translations.literal: Heng, following the Spring and Autumn principle that names do not take mountains and rivers, memorialized asking to change his name to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Spring and Autumn rule that names do not borrow mountains and rivers, Heng asked to change his name to Zhi.

sentences.zh: [5]歷位太常卿、中書監、侍中。

translations.literal: [5]By successive posts he was Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: [5]He rose to Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Secretariat, and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: Later he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅、司徒公，諡曰宣穆公。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Grand Tutor and Duke of the State, posthumous title Duke Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Duke of the State with the title Duke Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王小新成，和平二年封。

translations.literal: Xiao Xincheng, Prince of Jiyin, was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xincheng, Prince of Jiyin, received his fief in Heping year 2.

sentences.zh: 頗有武略。

translations.literal: He had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed real talent in war.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚侵擾，詔新成率眾討之。

translations.literal: When the Kumo Xi raided the borders, an edict ordered Xincheng to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kumo Xi raided the frontier, Xincheng was ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 新成乃多為毒酒，賊既漸逼，便棄營而去。

translations.literal: Xincheng made much poisoned wine; as the bandits pressed in he abandoned camp and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xincheng brewed great stores of poisoned wine; as the enemy closed in he abandoned camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊至，喜而競飲，聊無所備。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived they rejoiced and competed to drink, and for a time were wholly unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders came, drank eagerly, and for a while had no guard up.

sentences.zh: 遂簡輕騎，因醉縱擊，俘馘甚多。

translations.literal: He then chose light horse, and while they were drunk struck freely, taking many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: He then led light cavalry and struck the drunk camp, taking many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 後位外都大官。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of the Outer Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Director of the Outer Palace.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈大將軍，諡曰惠公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand General, posthumous title Duke Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand General with the title Duke Hui.

sentences.zh: 子鬱，字伏生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yu, styled Fusheng, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, courtesy name Fusheng, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 位開府。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank that opens the government.

sentences.zh: 為徐州刺史，以黷貨賜死，國除。

translations.literal: As inspector of Xuzhou, for corruption he was sentenced to death and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: As Xuzhou inspector he was executed for corruption and the fief abolished.

sentences.zh: 長子弼，字邕明，剛正有文學。

translations.literal: His eldest son Bi, styled Yongming, was upright and had literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bi, courtesy name Yongming, was upright and literate.

sentences.zh: 位中散大夫。

translations.literal: He held the post Central Scattered Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Central Scattered Grandee.

sentences.zh: 以世嫡應襲先爵，為季父尚書僕射麗因于氏親寵，遂奪弼王爵，撗授同母兄子誕。

translations.literal: As the legitimate heir he should have inherited the former title, but his uncle Li, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, through the Yu clan's favor seized Bi's princely title and forcibly gave it to his uterine brother's son Dan.
translations.idiomatic: As legitimate heir he should have taken the title, but his uncle Li, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, used the Yu family's favor to strip Bi and hand the fief to his uterine brother's son Dan.

sentences.zh: 於是弼絕棄人事，託疾還私第。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi wholly abandoned worldly affairs, pleaded illness, and returned to his private house.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then abandoned public life, pleaded illness, and withdrew to his house.

sentences.zh: 世宗徵為侍中，弼上表固讓。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned him as Palace Attendant; Bi memorialized firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong summoned him as Palace Attendant; Bi firmly declined by memorial.

sentences.zh: 入嵩山，以穴為室，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: He entered Mount Song, made a cave his chamber, and wore plain cloth and ate vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Mount Song, lived in a cave, and ate coarse greens in plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，子暉業訴復王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi, his son Huiye memorialized to restore the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyi year 1 his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely title.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，追贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the State, posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an year 3 he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the State with the title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 初，弼嘗夢人謂之曰：「君身不得傳世封，其紹先爵者，君長子紹遠也。

translations.literal: At first Bi once dreamed a man told him: "Your person cannot pass on a worldly fief; he who continues the former title will be your eldest son Shaoyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Bi once dreamed a voice saying, "You will not hold the fief in life; your eldest son Shaoyuan will restore the line."

sentences.zh: 」弼覺，即語暉業。

translations.literal: Bi awoke and at once told Huiye.
translations.idiomatic: He woke and told Huiye at once.

sentences.zh: 終如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it was as the words said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 暉業，少險薄，多與寇盜交通。

translations.literal: Huiye in youth was treacherous and shallow and often trafficked with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Huiye in youth was treacherous and shallow and trafficked with bandits.

sentences.zh: 長乃變節，涉子史，亦頗屬文，而慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: Growing older he changed his ways, studied the histories, also wrote somewhat, and was generous with resolute purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He later reformed, read histories, wrote a little, and grew generous and resolute.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太尉，加特進，領中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: By successive posts he was Duke of Works, Grand Marshal, with added special advancement, Director of the Secretariat, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Duke of Works and Grand Marshal, with special advancement, Director of the Secretariat, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄嘗問之曰：「比何所披覽？

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi once asked him: "What have you been reading lately?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi once asked him, "What have you been reading lately?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「數尋伊霍之傳，不讀曹馬之書。

translations.literal: He replied: "I often trace the stories of Yi and Huo; I do not read the books of Cao and Sima."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I keep to the tales of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of the Caos and Simas."

sentences.zh: 」暉業以時運漸謝，不復圖全，唯事飲啗，一日三羊，三日一犢。

translations.literal: Huiye, seeing the times gradually decline, no longer plotted to preserve himself whole but devoted himself only to eating and drinking—three sheep a day, a calf every three days.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the age fail, Huiye gave up saving himself whole and gave himself to feasting—three sheep a day, a calf every three days.

sentences.zh: 又嘗賦詩云：「昔居王道泰，濟濟富羣英。

translations.literal: He also once composed a poem: "Once the royal way was tranquil, and hosts of worthies flourished."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote: "Once the royal way was tranquil, and hosts of worthies flourished."

sentences.zh: 今逢世路阻，狐兔鬱縱橫。

translations.literal: Now we meet a blocked age, and foxes and hares throng unchecked."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the road is blocked, and foxes and hares run wild."

sentences.zh: 」齊初，降封美陽縣公，開府儀同三司、特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was demoted to Duke of Meiyang county, Opening the Government, Pillar of State, and special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's founding he was demoted to Duke of Meiyang county with the ranks Opening the Government, Pillar of State, and special advancement.

sentences.zh: 暉業之在晉陽也，無所交通，居常閑暇，乃撰魏藩王家世，號為辨宗室錄，四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: When Huiye was at Jinyang he kept no social ties; in his usual leisure he compiled the genealogies of Wei princes and kings, titled Records for Distinguishing the Imperial Clan, forty juan, and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he kept to himself; in idle hours he compiled the genealogies of Wei princes into the Records for Distinguishing the Imperial Clan in forty juan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 暉業弟昭業，頗有學尚，位諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye had considerable learning; he held the post Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Huiye's brother Zhaoye was learned and served as Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 莊帝將幸洛南，昭業立於閶闔門外，扣馬諫，帝避之而過，後勞勉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was about to visit the southern capital, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed by, then later comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang meant to visit the southern capital, Zhaoye stood at the Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor passed around him, then later praised him.

sentences.zh: 位給事黃門侍郎、衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the posts Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Guards General, and Right Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Guards General, and Right Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 鬱弟偃，字仲琁，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Yan, styled Zhongxuan, held the post Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's brother Yan, courtesy name Zhongxuan, was Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子撫，字伯懿，襲。

translations.literal: His son Fu, styled Boyi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Boyi, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，為從兄暉業訴奪王爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhuang's reign he was made to petition through his cousin Huiye to recover the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhuang's reign he petitioned through his cousin Huiye to recover the princely title.

sentences.zh: 拜雍州刺史，為政嚴酷，吏人患之。

translations.literal: Made inspector of Yongzhou, his government was harsh and cruel, and officials and people suffered under it.
translations.idiomatic: As Yongzhou inspector he ruled with harsh cruelty, and officials and people groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 其妻崔氏誕一男，麗遂出州獄囚死及徒流案未申臺者，一時放免。

translations.literal: When his wife Lady Cui bore a son, Li at once released from the provincial prison those condemned to death and all exiles and convicts whose cases had not yet reached the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Cui bore a son, Li emptied the provincial prison of the condemned and every exile whose case had not yet reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷冀州刺史，入為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Transferred to inspector of Jizhou, he entered the capital as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Jizhou, he then entered the capital as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「聞公在州，殺戮無理，枉濫非一，又大殺道人。

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "I hear that in the province you killed without reason, wronged many, and also killed many monks in great numbers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hear that in your province you killed without cause, wronged many, and slaughtered monks in great numbers."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣在冀州可殺道人二百許人，亦復何多？

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant in Jizhou could kill only about two hundred monks—how is that many?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In Jizhou I killed only some two hundred monks—how is that many?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「一物不得其所，若納諸隍，況殺道人二百而言不多。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If one creature does not obtain its place, it is as though one were cast into a moat—how much more when two hundred monks are killed and you say it is not many."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If a single creature is wronged it is as though cast into a ditch—how then when two hundred monks die and you call it few?"

sentences.zh: 」麗脫冠謝，賜坐。

translations.literal: Li removed his cap and apologized; he was granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Li doffed his cap and apologized; he was given a seat.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wei.

sentences.zh: 子顯和，少有節操，歷司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xianhe in youth had integrity; he held the post Recorder of the Masters of Writing in the Department of State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianhe in youth had integrity and served as Recorder in the Department of State.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔光每見之曰：「元參軍風流清秀，容止閑雅，乃宰相之器。

translations.literal: Every time Minister of Education Cui Guang saw him he would say: "Adjutant Yuan is refined and clear in bearing, leisurely and elegant in deportment—the stuff of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cui Guang, Minister of Education, met him, he said, "Adjutant Yuan is graceful and poised—born to stand at the head of the government."

sentences.zh: 」除徐州安東府長史。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Chief Administrator of the Andong sub-office in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made chief administrator of Xuzhou's Andong sub-office.

sentences.zh: 刺史元法僧叛，顯和與戰被擒，執手命與連坐。

translations.literal: The inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled; Xianhe fought him, was captured, and Faseng took his hand and ordered him to sit in joint punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Yuan Faseng rose in rebellion, Xianhe fought him, was taken, and Faseng seized his hand and bade him share the bench of the condemned.

sentences.zh: 顯和曰：「顯和與阿翁同源別派，皆是盤石之宗，一朝以地外叛，若遇董狐，能無慚德。

translations.literal: Xianhe said: "Xianhe and my elder uncle share one source but different branches—both are clans as firm as bedrock. Yet in a single morning you rebel with your territory. Before a recorder like Dong Hu, could your virtue not blush?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe said, "My uncle and I spring from one root, though our lines diverge—we are both bedrock of the house. Yet in one morning you cast your land to rebellion. Faced with Dong Hu's brush, how could your honor not burn?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不肯坐。

translations.literal: He would not sit.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to sit.

sentences.zh: 法僧猶欲慰喻，顯和曰：「乃可死作惡鬼，不能坐為叛臣。

translations.literal: Faseng still wished to comfort and persuade him; Xianhe said: "I would rather die and become an evil ghost than sit as a rebel minister."
translations.idiomatic: Faseng still tried to soothe him; Xianhe said, "I would sooner die a vengeful ghost than sit among rebel ministers."

sentences.zh: 」及將殺之，神色自若。

translations.literal: When they were about to kill him, his expression was composed.
translations.idiomatic: When the moment of execution came, his face did not change.

sentences.zh: 建義初，贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was posthumously made Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 汝陰王天賜，和平三年封，[6]拜鎮南大將軍、虎牢鎮都大將。

translations.literal: Yin Prince Tianci [6] was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and appointed Great General Who Guards the South and Grand Commander of the Tiger Cage Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tianci of Ru'nan was enfeoffed in Heping year 3 [6] and named Great General Who Guards the South and grand commander of the Tiger Cage garrison.

sentences.zh: 後為內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he became Grand Inner Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand Inner Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，殿中尚書胡莫寒簡西部敕勒豪富兼丁者為殿中武士，而大納財貨，簡選不平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, Palace Director Hu Mohen of the Hall of the Center simplified the wealthy of the western Tiele tribes who also held military households into palace warriors, while taking bribes in great quantity and making selections unfairly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign, Hu Mohen, Director of the Hall of the Center, culled wealthy western Tiele households with military obligations into palace guards—and took heavy bribes, choosing unfairly.

sentences.zh: 眾怒，殺莫寒及高平假鎮將奚陵，於是諸部敕勒悉叛。

translations.literal: The masses were enraged and killed Mohen and Xi Ling, acting commander of the Gao Ping garrison, whereupon all Tiele tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rose in fury, killed Mohen and Xi Ling, acting commander at Gao Ping, and every Tiele division rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔天賜與給事中羅雲督諸軍討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tianci and Attendant-within-the-Palace Luo Yun to supervise the armies in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Tianci and Luo Yun, attendant-within-the-palace, to lead the armies against them.

sentences.zh: 前鋒敕勒詐降，雲信之，副將元伏曰：「敕勒色動，恐將有變，今不設備，將為所圖。

translations.literal: The vanguard Tiele feigned surrender; Yun believed them. Vice-commander Yuan Fu said: "The Tiele look unsettled—there may be a plot. If we make no preparations now, we shall be trapped."
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele vanguard pretended to submit; Yun trusted them. Vice-commander Yuan Fu said, "Their faces shift—they may turn. Without precautions we will be ambushed."

sentences.zh: 」雲不從。

translations.literal: Yun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 敕勒輕騎數千襲殺雲，天賜僅得自全。

translations.literal: Several thousand Tiele light horsemen raided and killed Yun; Tianci barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Tiele light horse struck and killed Yun; Tianci barely got away alive.

sentences.zh: 後除征北大將軍、護匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: Later he was made Great General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel Protector of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Great General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel Protector of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 累遷懷朔鎮大將，坐貪殘，恕死，削除官爵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commander of Huaishuo Garrison, then punished for greed and cruelty—death was remitted and his offices and titles were struck.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand commander of Huaishuo Garrison, then was condemned for rapacity and cruelty; execution was remitted but rank and titles were stripped.

sentences.zh: 卒，高祖哭於思政觀，贈本爵，葬從王禮，諡曰靈王。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Gaozu wept at the Hall of Governance and Thought, posthumously restored his original title, buried him with princely rites, and gave the posthumous name Prince Ling.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Gaozu wept at the Hall of Governance and Thought, restored his original title in death, buried him with princely honors, and styled him Prince Ling.

sentences.zh: 子逞，字萬安。

translations.literal: His son Cheng, styled Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng, styled Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 卒於齊州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died as Inspector of Qi Province; posthumous name Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died as inspector of Qi Province and was posthumously styled Wei.

sentences.zh: 逞子慶和，東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Cheng's son Qinghe was Inspector of East Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's son Qinghe became Inspector of East Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 為蕭衍將所攻，舉城降之。

translations.literal: When attacked by a general of Xiao Yan, he surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Attacked by one of Xiao Yan's generals, he surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 衍以為北道總督、魏王。

translations.literal: Yan made him Northern Route Commander-in-Chief and Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan made him commander-in-chief of the northern route and Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 至項城，朝廷出師討之，望風退走。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangcheng the court sent troops against him; at sight of them he fled.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Xiangcheng; the court marched against him; he fled at the first wind of their banners.

sentences.zh: 衍責之曰：「言同百舌，膽若鼷鼠。

translations.literal: Yan rebuked him: "Your words run with a hundred tongues, your courage is that of a field mouse."
translations.idiomatic: Yan scolded him: "You speak with a hundred tongues and fight with a mouse's heart."

sentences.zh: 」遂徙合浦。

translations.literal: He was then banished to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 逞弟汎，字普安。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Fan, styled Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Fan, styled Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 自元士稍遷營州刺史。

translations.literal: From Prince of the Blood he was gradually promoted to Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: From prince of the blood he rose step by step to Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 性貪殘，人不堪命，相率逐之，汎走平州。

translations.literal: Greedy and cruel by nature, the people could not bear his rule and drove him out together; Fan fled to Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: His greed and cruelty drove the people to rise together and expel him; Fan fled to Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 後除光祿大夫、宗正卿，封東燕縣男。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed as Baron of Dongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed Baron of Dongyan.

sentences.zh: 於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: He met his death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 天賜第五子脩義，字壽安，涉獵書傳，頗有文才，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Tianci's fifth son Xiuyi, styled Shou'an, ranged widely in books and records and had considerable literary talent; Emperor Gaozu took note of him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianci's fifth son Xiuyi, styled Shou'an, read widely and wrote well; Gaozu noticed him.

sentences.zh: 自元士稍遷左將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: From Prince of the Blood he was gradually promoted to Left General and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: From prince of the blood he rose to Left General and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 脩義以齊州頻喪刺史，累表固辭。

translations.literal: Xiuyi, because Qi Province had repeatedly lost its inspectors, memorialized again and again to decline firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had lost one inspector after another; Xiuyi memorialized again and again to refuse the post.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「修短有命，吉凶由人，何得過致憂憚，以乖維城之寄。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Length of life has its fate, fortune and misfortune lie in men—how can you heap up fear beyond measure and fail the charge of guarding the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Life's span is fated; luck rests in the living—why heap fear on fear and betray the charge to guard the realm?"

sentences.zh: 違凶就吉，時亦有之，可聽更立館宇。

translations.literal: Turning from misfortune toward fortune also happens in its season; you may build new offices."
translations.idiomatic: Turning ill fortune to good has its seasons; you may build new offices."

sentences.zh: 」於是移理東城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved his seat of government to the eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his administration to the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 脩義為政，寬和愛人，在州四歲，不殺一人，百姓以是追思之。

translations.literal: Xiuyi's government was lenient and he loved the people; in four years in the province he killed not a single man, and the common people for that reason cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi governed gently and loved the people; in four years he executed no one, and the province mourned him when he left.

sentences.zh: 遷秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，表陳庶人禧、庶人愉等，請宥前愆，賜葬陵域。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he memorialized on the commoners Xi and Yu and others, asking pardon for past faults and burial within the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong came to the throne he memorialized for the degraded princes Xi and Yu, asking pardon and burial in the imperial necropolis.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔曰：「收葬之恩，事由上旨，藩岳何得越職干陳！

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling issued an edict: "The grace of receiving burial rests with the sovereign's intent—how may a frontier prince overstep his office and press such a petition!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling replied, "Burial is the sovereign's gift—how may a border prince overstep and plead it?"

sentences.zh: 」在州多受納。

translations.literal: In the province he took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In office he took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及在銓衡，唯專貨賄，授官大小，皆有定價。

translations.literal: Once he held the scales of appointment he dealt only in bribes; every office great or small had a fixed price.
translations.idiomatic: At the helm of appointments he sold every office; great and small posts each had their price.

sentences.zh: 時中散大夫高居者，有旨先敍，時上黨郡缺，居遂求之。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Attendant Ju Gao had an edict for prior promotion; the Shangdang commandery post was vacant and Ju sought it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Ju Gao had been slated for early promotion; when Shangdang commandery fell vacant, Ju asked for it.

sentences.zh: 脩義私已許人，抑居不與。

translations.literal: Xiuyi had privately already promised the post to another and refused Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi had already promised the post elsewhere and denied Ju.

sentences.zh: 居大言不遜，脩義命左右牽曳之。

translations.literal: Ju spoke insolently; Xiuyi ordered his attendants to drag him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju shouted abuse; Xiuyi had attendants haul him away.

sentences.zh: 居對大眾呼天唱賊。

translations.literal: Ju cried to Heaven before the assembly and called out "Thief!"
translations.idiomatic: Before the whole court Ju cried to Heaven and called him a thief.

sentences.zh: 人問居曰：「白日公庭，安得有賊？

translations.literal: Someone asked Ju: "In broad daylight in the public hall, how can there be a thief?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Ju, "In open court at noon—where is the thief?"

sentences.zh: 」居指脩義曰：「此座上者，違天子明詔，物多者得官，京師白劫，此非大賊乎？

translations.literal: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said: "The man on that seat defies the Son of Heaven's clear edict—whoever brings the most goods gets office; daylight robbery in the capital—is that not a great thief?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said, "That man on the dais defies the Son of Heaven—richest bidder wins rank; this is open robbery in the capital—is he not the thief?"

sentences.zh: 」脩義失色。

translations.literal: Xiuyi lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi's face went white.

sentences.zh: 居行罵而出。

translations.literal: Ju went out still cursing.
translations.idiomatic: Ju left still shouting curses.

sentences.zh: 後欲邀車駕論脩義罪狀，左僕射蕭寶夤諭之，乃止。

translations.literal: Later he wished to intercept the imperial carriage to lay out Xiuyi's crimes; Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin persuaded him and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later he meant to waylay the imperial carriage and accuse Xiuyi; Xiao Baoyin, Left Vice Director, talked him down.

sentences.zh: 二秦反，假脩義兼尚書右僕射、西道行臺、行秦州事，為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: When the Two Qins rebelled, Xiuyi was given concurrent appointment as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Western Route Grand Mobile Office, and acting Qin Province affairs, with command over all armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Qins rose, Xiuyi was made concurrent Right Vice Director, Western Route grand mobile office, and acting governor of Qin, commanding the armies.

sentences.zh: 脩義性好酒，每飲連日，遂遇風病，神明昏喪，雖至長安，竟無部分之益。

translations.literal: Xiuyi was fond of wine and drank for days on end; he then contracted wind illness, his mind clouded, and though he reached Chang'an he brought no benefit of command at all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi loved wine and drank for days; wind sickness struck, his mind dimmed, and even at Chang'an he could not command.

sentences.zh: 元志敗沒，賊東至黑水，更遣蕭寶夤討之，以脩義為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhi was defeated and lost; the rebels advanced east to Blackwater; Xiao Baoyin was again sent to suppress them, with Xiuyi made Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhi was destroyed; rebels reached Blackwater; Baoyin was sent again, and Xiuyi made Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，[7]贈司空，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died in the province [7] and was posthumously made Minister of Works; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office [7], was posthumously made Minister of Works, and styled Wen.

sentences.zh: 子均，位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Jun held office as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 樂浪王萬壽，和平三年封，拜征東大將軍，鎮和龍。

translations.literal: Prince Wanshou of Lelang was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the East, and stationed at Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wanshou of Lelang was enfeoffed in Heping year 3, made Great General Who Pacifies the East, and garrisoned Helong.

sentences.zh: 性貪暴，徵還，道憂薨。

translations.literal: Greedy and violent by nature, he was recalled and died of grief on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and brutal, he was recalled and died of grief on the road.

sentences.zh: 諡曰厲王。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name: Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 子康王樂平，襲。

translations.literal: His son Prince Le Ping of Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Prince Le Ping of Kang, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子長命，襲。

translations.literal: His son Changming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changming succeeded.

sentences.zh: 坐殺人賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Punished with mandated death for murder; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned to death for murder; the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 子忠，肅宗時，復前爵，位太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhong, in Emperor Suzong's time, had the former title restored and held office as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong, under Suzong, recovered the old title and became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 出帝汎舟天淵池，命宗室諸王陪宴。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu boated on the Celestial Abyss Pool and ordered the princes of the imperial clan to attend the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chu drifted on the Celestial Abyss Pool and summoned the clan princes to feast.

sentences.zh: 忠愚而無智，性好衣服，遂著紅羅襦，繡作領，碧紬袴，錦為緣。

translations.literal: Zhong was stupid and without wisdom, fond of clothes by nature; he therefore wore a red gauze jacket with embroidered collar, indigo silk trousers, and brocade trim.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was dull and witless, mad for dress; he came in red gauze with an embroidered collar, indigo trousers, brocade hems.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「朝廷衣冠，應有常式，何為著百戲衣？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Court dress should have a fixed form—why wear the costume of variety performers?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Court dress has its form—why come in acrobat's colors?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「臣少來所愛，情存綺羅，歌衣舞服，是臣所願。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "What I have loved since youth lives in brocade and gauze; song-robes and dance-garments are my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "Since boyhood I have loved silk and gauze; singing robes and dancing dress are all I ask."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「人之無良，乃至此乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For a man to be so without decency—it has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To lack decency so utterly—how far you have fallen!"

sentences.zh: 廣平王洛侯，和平二年封。

translations.literal: Prince Luohou of Guangping was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Luohou of Guangping was enfeoffed in Heping year 2.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰殤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous name Shang.

sentences.zh: 無子，後以陽平幽王第五子匡後之。

translations.literal: Having no son, later the fifth son of Prince You of Yangping, Kuang, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; later Kuang, fifth son of Prince You of Yangping, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 匡字建扶，性耿介，有氣節。

translations.literal: Kuang, styled Jianfu, was upright by nature and had spirit and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, styled Jianfu, was stiff-backed by nature, with spirit and backbone.

sentences.zh: 高祖器之[8]謂曰：「叔父必能儀形社稷，匡輔朕躬，今可改名為匡，以成克終之美。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu valued him [8] and said: "Uncle, you will surely give form to the altars of state and steady my person; you may now change your name to Kuang, to fulfill the beauty of seeing things through to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu favored him [8] and said, "Uncle, you will brace the altars and steady my throne; take the name Kuang now, that you may finish what you begin."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Kuang was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded, Kuang rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 茹皓始有寵，百僚微憚之。

translations.literal: Ru Hao first gained favor; the hundred officials slightly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Hao first won favor; officials learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 世宗曾於山陵還，詔匡陪乘，又命皓登車。

translations.literal: Shizong once returned from the imperial tombs, ordered Kuang to ride beside him, and also commanded Hao to mount the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the tombs, Shizong set Kuang beside him and told Hao to mount the carriage too.

sentences.zh: 皓褰裳將上，匡諫止，世宗推之令下，皓恨匡失色。

translations.literal: Hao lifted his robe to ascend; Kuang remonstrated and stopped him; Shizong pushed Hao down; Hao hated Kuang and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Hao gathered his skirts to climb in; Kuang barred him; Shizong shoved Hao down; Hao glared, bloodless.

sentences.zh: 當時壯其忠謇。

translations.literal: At the time people admired his loyal bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time praised his blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，除肆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shizong took personal rule, Kuang was made Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the reins himself, Kuang was made Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 匡既忤皓，懼為所害，廉慎自修，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Kuang having already offended Hao, feared harm from him, cultivated integrity and caution, and had a strong reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Having crossed Hao, Kuang feared assassination, tightened his conduct, and won a name for clean rule.

sentences.zh: 遷恒州刺史，徵為大宗正卿、河南邑中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Heng Province and summoned as Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and Rectifier of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Heng Province, then recalled as Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and rectifier of Henan.

sentences.zh: 匡奏親王及始藩、二藩王妻悉有妃號，而三藩已下皆謂之妻，上不得同為妃名，而下不及五品已上有命婦之號，竊為疑。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized that the wives of imperial princes and of the first- and second-rank princedoms all bore the title consort, while third-rank princedoms and below were only called wives—above they could not share the title consort, yet below they did not reach the titled ladies of fifth rank and above; he privately found this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang argued that first- and second-rank princes' wives were consorts, but third rank and below were merely "wives"—too low to share "consort," yet above the titled ladies of fifth rank—and asked that the rule be clarified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫貴於朝，妻榮於室，婦女無定，升從其夫。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the husband is honored at court, the wife is glorified in the chamber; a woman's standing is not fixed—she rises with her husband."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Honor the man at court and the wife shines at home; a woman's rank is not fixed—she rises with her husband."

sentences.zh: 三藩既啟王封，妃名亦宜同等。

translations.literal: The third-rank princedoms having opened royal enfeoffment, the title consort should likewise be equal.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank princes now hold royal fiefs; their wives should share the title consort.

sentences.zh: 妻者，齊也，理與己齊，可從妃例。

translations.literal: Wife means equal; in principle she is equal to oneself—she may follow the consort precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Wife means equal; in principle she stands level with her lord—let her follow the consort rule."

sentences.zh: 」自是三藩王妻名號始定。

translations.literal: From then on the titles of third-rank princes' wives were first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: From then the titles of third-rank princes' wives were fixed.

sentences.zh: 後除度支尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 匡表引樂陵、章武之例，求紹洛侯封，詔付尚書議。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized citing the precedents of Leling and Zhangwu, asking to continue Prince Luohou's fief; the edict was referred to the Masters of Writing for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang cited Leling and Zhangwu and asked to revive Luohou's fief; the matter went to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏聽襲封，以明興絕之義。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized permission to inherit the fief, to make clear the principle of reviving extinct lines.
translations.idiomatic: They recommended allowing succession, to show the principle of reviving extinct lines.

sentences.zh: 匡與尚書令高肇不平，常無降下之色。

translations.literal: Kuang was at odds with Director Gao Zhao and never showed a submissive bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang clashed with Director Gao Zhao and never bowed his head.

sentences.zh: 時世宗委政於肇，朝廷傾憚，唯匡與肇抗衡。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong entrusted government to Zhao; the court leaned in fear, and only Kuang stood against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong left power to Zhao; the court bent before him—only Kuang held the line.

sentences.zh: 先自造棺，置於廳事，意欲輿棺詣闕，論肇罪惡，自殺切諫。
