translations.literal: He had first built a coffin for himself and placed it in the main hall, intending to carry the coffin to the palace gates, lay out Zhao's crimes, and kill himself in desperate remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He had built his own coffin and set it in the hall, meaning to haul it to the gates, denounce Zhao, and die in protest.

sentences.zh: 肇聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Zhao heard of it and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao heard and hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 後因與太常劉芳議爭權量，遂與肇聲色。

translations.literal: Later, because of disputing weights and measures with Grand Director of Imperial Sacrifices Liu Fang, he came to open quarrel with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he quarreled with Liu Fang over weights and measures and fell into open feud with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯奏匡曰：

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian memorialized against Kuang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian accused Kuang, writing:

sentences.zh: 自金行失御，羣偽競興，禮壞樂崩，彝倫攸斁。

translations.literal: Since the Metal Line lost the reins, many false regimes rose in rivalry; rites were broken and music collapsed, and the great norms were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin lost the mandate, pretenders multiplied; ritual and music shattered and the great norms fell.

sentences.zh: 大魏應期，奄有四海。

translations.literal: Great Wei answered the age and embraced all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei rose to its season and took the realm within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝以睿聖統天，克復舊典。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen the Filial and Cultured, with sage wisdom ruling Heaven, restored the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, sage and cultured, ruled with heaven's wit and restored the old canons.

sentences.zh: 乃命故中書監高閭廣旌儒林，推尋樂府，依据六經，參諸國志，以黍裁寸，將均周漢舊章。

translations.literal: He then ordered the former Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lu to proclaim widely in the Confucian schools, search out the Music Bureau, take the Six Classics as basis and consult the histories of the states, cut the inch from millet, and balance the old statutes of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered former Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu to scour the schools, recover the Music Bureau, ground the work in the Six Classics and state histories, cut the inch from millet grain, and align Zhou and Han measure.

sentences.zh: 屬雲構中遷，尚未云就。

translations.literal: But as the cloud-frame capital was still moving, the work was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was still on the move; the work was not finished.

sentences.zh: 高祖睿思玄深，參考經記，以一黍之大，用成分體，準之為尺，宣布施行。

translations.literal: The emperor's wise thought was profound and abstruse; consulting classics and records, he used one millet's size to form the whole body, took it as standard for the foot, and proclaimed and enacted it.
translations.idiomatic: His thought ran deep; from the classics he took one millet-grain as module for the whole foot, made it law, and proclaimed it.

sentences.zh: 暨正始中，故太樂令公孫崇輒自立意，以黍十二為寸，別造尺度，定律刊鍾。

translations.literal: By the Zhengshi era the former Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong on his own set up a scheme, making twelve millet for the inch and separately forging measure and pitch, fixing the law and casting bells.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi, former Director of Imperial Music Gongsun Chong devised his own scheme—twelve millet to the inch—new measure, new pitch, new bells.

sentences.zh: 皆向成訖，表求觀試。

translations.literal: All were finished in one direction; he memorialized requesting inspection and trial.
translations.idiomatic: When all was ready he asked for trial before the court.

sentences.zh: 時敕太常卿臣芳，以崇造既成，請集朝英，議其得否。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Grand Director of Imperial Sacrifices Fang to gather the court's worthies, since Chong's work was done, and debate whether it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told Grand Director Fang to assemble the court's experts and judge Chong's finished work.

sentences.zh: 芳疑崇尺度與先朝不同，察其作者，於經史復異，推造尠據，非所宜行。

translations.literal: Fang doubted that Chong's measure differed from the prior dynasty's, examined its makers against classics and histories and found further discrepancy, judged the forging thinly grounded, and held it should not be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Fang found Chong's foot unlike the prior dynasty's, checked makers against the classics, found the basis thin, and said it must not pass.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令臣肇、清河王懌等以崇造乖謬，與周禮不同，遂奏臣芳依周禮更造，成訖量校，從其善者。

translations.literal: At that time Director Zhao, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and others held Chong's forging mistaken and unlike the Rites of Zhou; they memorialized that Fang should remake according to the Rites of Zhou, and when finished compare measures and follow whichever was better.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Prince Yi of Qinghe, and others said Chong erred against the Zhou Rites and urged Fang to remake by Zhou measure, then compare and take the better.

sentences.zh: 而芳以先朝尺度，事合古典。

translations.literal: But Fang held that the prior dynasty's measure accorded with the ancient canon.
translations.idiomatic: Fang held the old foot already matched antiquity.

sentences.zh: 乃依前詔書，以黍刊寸，並呈朝廷，用裁金石。

translations.literal: He therefore followed the earlier edict, cut the inch from millet, and presented it to the court to trim metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the earlier edict, cut the inch from millet, and presented it to tune bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 于時議者，多云芳是，唯黃門侍郎臣孫惠蔚與崇扶同。

translations.literal: Among debaters at the time many said Fang was right; only Yellow Gate Attendant Sun Huiwei sided with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Most debaters sided with Fang; only Sun Huiwei, Yellow Gate Attendant, backed Chong.

sentences.zh: 二途參差，頻經考議。

translations.literal: The two paths diverged and were repeatedly examined in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Two paths diverged; debate ran again and again.

sentences.zh: 而尚書令臣肇以芳造。

translations.literal: And Director Zhao favored Fang's forging.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhao favored what Fang had made.

sentences.zh: 崇物故之後，而惠蔚亦造一尺，仍云扶。

translations.literal: After Chong died, Huiwei also forged a foot, still claiming support.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong died, Huiwei forged another foot and still claimed his own side.

sentences.zh: [9]以比崇尺，自相乖背。

translations.literal: [9] Compared with Chong's foot, they contradicted each other.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Laid beside Chong's foot, the two measures contradicted each other.

sentences.zh: 量省二三，謂芳為得。

translations.literal: Measuring and checking, two or three points favored Fang as correct.
translations.idiomatic: On measurement, two or three tests favored Fang.

sentences.zh: 而尚書臣匡表云劉孫二尺，長短相傾，稽考兩律，所容殊異。

translations.literal: But Kuang of the Masters of Writing memorialized that Liu's and Sun's two feet, long and short leaning against each other, when examined against the two pitch laws contained markedly different capacities.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang of the Masters of Writing wrote that Liu's foot and Sun's foot tilted against each other, and when tested against the two pitch laws their capacities diverged sharply.

sentences.zh: 言取中黍，校彼二家，云並參差，抑中無所，[10]自立一途，請求議判。

translations.literal: He said to take the middle millet and compare the two houses, declaring both divergent with no middle ground [10], establishing his own path and asking for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed a middle millet, compared both schools, found neither sound [10], set his own path, and asked the court to decide.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，或是於匡。

translations.literal: Among debaters at the time some sided with Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Some debaters then sided with Kuang.

sentences.zh: 兩途舛駁，未即時定。

translations.literal: The two paths clashed and were not settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: The quarrel collided and was not settled.

sentences.zh: 肇又云，權斛斗尺，班行已久，今者所論，豈喻先旨。

translations.literal: Zhao also said that weights, bushels, dou, and feet had been promulgated long since; what was now debated could hardly match the prior intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said weights, bushels, and feet had long been law—today's quarrel could not match the old intent.

sentences.zh: 宜仰依先朝故尺為定。

translations.literal: One should respectfully follow the prior dynasty's old foot as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The prior dynasty's foot should stand as fixed.

sentences.zh: 自爾以後，而匡與肇厲言都座，聲色相加，高下失其常倫，噂競無復彝序。

translations.literal: From then on Kuang and Zhao spoke harshly in the chief seat, voices and faces adding against each other; high and low lost their constant order, and clamor no longer kept ritual sequence.
translations.idiomatic: After that Kuang and Zhao shouted across the chief seat; rank lost its order and debate lost its ritual.

sentences.zh: 匡更表列，據己十是，云芳十非。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized again in columns, holding his own ten points true and Fang's ten false.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang listed charges again: his ten points true, Fang's ten false.

sentences.zh: 又云：「肇前被敕旨，共芳營督，規立鍾石之名，希播製作之譽。

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhao earlier received the edict to supervise with Fang, planning the names of bells and stones, hoping to spread the reputation of making them."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote, "Zhao was edicted to supervise with Fang, to name the bells and stones and win the fame of their making."

sentences.zh: 乃憑樞衡之尊，藉舅氏之勢，與奪任心，臧否自己。

translations.literal: He relied on the dignity of the pivot-scale and borrowed his maternal clan's power; grant and denial followed his heart, praise and blame were his own.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on the minister's scale and his kin's power; grant and denial, praise and blame, were his alone.

sentences.zh: 阿黨劉芳，遏絕臣事，望勢雷同者接以恩言，依經按古者即被怒責。

translations.literal: He curried favor with Liu Fang, blocked my business, greeted those who echoed his power with kind words, and raged at those who checked against the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He favored Liu Fang, blocked my work, flattered those who echoed him, and raged at those who held to the classics.

sentences.zh: 雖未指鹿化馬，移天徙日，實使蘊藉之士，聳氣坐端，懷道之夫，結舌筵次。

translations.literal: Though he had not yet turned deer into horses or moved heaven and shifted the sun, he truly made reserved scholars draw up their breath at their seats and men who kept the Way bite their tongues at the mats.
translations.idiomatic: He had not yet turned deer to horses or moved heaven—but reserved scholars held their breath at court and honest men bit their tongues at the feast.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「芳昔與崇競，恒言自作，今共臣論，忽稱先朝。

translations.literal: He also said: "Fang once competed with Chong and always said he made things himself; now debating with me he suddenly calls on the prior dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Fang once fought Chong and called every measure his own; now, debating me, he hides behind the prior dynasty."

sentences.zh: 豈不前謂可行，輒欲自取，後知錯謬，便推先朝。

translations.literal: Was it not that he first said it could be done and wished to take it for himself, then knowing it wrong pushed it onto the prior dynasty?
translations.idiomatic: First he said his scheme would work and meant to claim it; when error showed, he pushed it on the old emperors.

sentences.zh: 殊非大臣之體，深失為下之義。

translations.literal: This is far from the bearing of a great minister and deeply fails the duty of a subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: That is not how great ministers behave, nor how subordinates should serve.

sentences.zh: 復考校勢臣之前，量度偏頗之手，臣必刖足內朝，抱璞人外。

translations.literal: If I again examine before the powerful minister and the partial hand that skewed measure, I shall surely lose my feet within the inner court and embrace jade outside among men."
translations.idiomatic: Before power's skewed hand I shall lose my feet in court and carry jade in the street."

sentences.zh: 」囂言肆意，彰於朝野。

translations.literal: Wild words ran at will and showed plainly through court and market.
translations.idiomatic: His wild words rang through court and market.

sentences.zh: 然匡職當出納，獻替所在，斗尺權度，正是所司。

translations.literal: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and delivery, and remonstrance was his place; weights, bushels, and measure were precisely his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and remonstrance—and weights and measures were his office.

sentences.zh: 若己有所見，能練臧否，宜應首唱義端，早辨諸惑，何故默心隨從，不關一言，見芳成事，方有此語。

translations.literal: If he had his own view and could judge right and wrong, he should have led with righteous argument early and distinguished the doubts—why keep silent and follow, not speaking one word, and only after Fang's work was done utter these words?
translations.idiomatic: If he truly saw the flaw he should have spoken when it mattered—why stay silent until Fang succeeded, then cry fraud?

sentences.zh: 計芳才學，與匡殊懸，所見淺深，不應相匹。

translations.literal: Considering Fang's talent and learning, it cannot be hung with Kuang's; the shallow and deep of their views should not be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's learning towers above Kuang's; their depth cannot be compared.

sentences.zh: 今乃始發，恐此由心，[11]借智於人，規成虛譽。

translations.literal: Now he speaks only at the end—I fear this comes from the heart [11], borrowing another's wit to seek empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Now he speaks late—I fear vanity [11], borrowing others' wit for hollow fame.

sentences.zh: 況匡表云：「所據銅權，形如古誌，明是漢作，非莽別造。

translations.literal: Moreover Kuang's memorial said: "The bronze weight he relies on is shaped like the ancient record—clearly Han work, not a separate forging of Mang."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang also said his bronze weight matched the ancient record—clearly Han, not Mang's new forge.

sentences.zh: 」及案權銘云：「黃帝始袓，德布於虞，虞帝始袓，德布於新。

translations.literal: And examining the weight's inscription: "The Yellow Emperor's first ancestor—his virtue spread to Yu; Yu the Emperor's first ancestor—his virtue spread to Xin."
translations.idiomatic: The inscription read: "Yellow Emperor's first ancestor, virtue to Yu; Yu the Emperor's first ancestor, virtue to Xin."

sentences.zh: 」若莽佐漢時事，寧有銘偽新之號哉。

translations.literal: If Mang assisted Han in his time, how could there be an inscription with the false name Xin?
translations.idiomatic: If Mang served Han, why would the inscription bear the false name Xin?

sentences.zh: 又尋莽傳云，莽居攝，即變漢制度。

translations.literal: Searching further Mang's biography: when Mang held the regency he at once changed Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Mang's biography says that in regency he changed Han institutions at once.

sentences.zh: 考校二證，非漢權明矣。

translations.literal: Checking the two proofs, it is clear it is not a Han weight.
translations.idiomatic: The two proofs show it is no Han weight.

sentences.zh: 復云：「芳之所造，又短先朝之尺。

translations.literal: He also said: "What Fang forged is again shorter than the prior dynasty's foot."
translations.idiomatic: He also said Fang's foot falls short of the prior dynasty's.

sentences.zh: 」臣既比之，權然相合。

translations.literal: Your subject has compared them—the weight agrees exactly.
translations.idiomatic: I compared them—the weight matches exactly.

sentences.zh: 更云：「芳尺與千金堰不同。

translations.literal: He further said: "Fang's foot differs from the Qianjin weir."
translations.idiomatic: He further said Fang's foot differs from the Qianjin weir mark.

sentences.zh: 」臣復量比，因見其異。

translations.literal: Your subject again measured and compared and thereupon saw the difference.
translations.idiomatic: I measured again and saw the difference.

sentences.zh: 二三浮濫，難可據準。

translations.literal: Two or three floating excesses—hard to take as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Two or three loose points—too weak to serve as standard.

sentences.zh: 又云：「共構虛端，妄為疑似，託以先朝，云非己製。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Together they built a false edge, recklessly made suspected forms, and lodged it on the prior dynasty, saying it was not their own making."
translations.idiomatic: He also charged them with forging doubt and pinning it on the prior dynasty, saying it was not their work.

sentences.zh: 臣按此欺詐，乃在於匡，不在於芳。

translations.literal: Your subject finds this deceit lies in Kuang, not in Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The deceit is Kuang's, not Fang's.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 芳先被敕，專造鍾律，管籥優劣，是其所裁，權斛尺度，本非其事。

translations.literal: Fang was first edicted to specialize in forging bells and pitch; the excellence of pipes and reeds was his to trim—weights, bushels, and measure were originally not his affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was edicted to make bells and pitch; pipes were his—but weights and bushels were never his charge.

sentences.zh: 比前門下索芳尺度，而芳牒報云：「依先朝所班新尺，復應下黍，更不增損，為造鍾律，調正分寸而已。

translations.literal: Earlier the Secretariat sought Fang's measure and Fang replied in a document: "Following the prior dynasty's promulgated new foot, again applying lower millet without further increase or decrease—only to tune bells and pitch and adjust inches and parts."
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat asked his measure, Fang replied: "I follow the prior dynasty's promulgated foot, lower millet unchanged—only tuning bells and pitch."

sentences.zh: 」檢匡造時在牒後一歲，芳於爾日，匡未共爭，已有此牒，豈為詐也？

translations.literal: Checking Kuang's forging—it was one year after that document; on that day Kuang had not yet disputed with Fang and this document already existed—how could it be fraud?
translations.idiomatic: Kuang forged his measure a year later; that day he had not yet quarreled with Fang—the document already existed; where is the fraud?

sentences.zh: 計崇造寸，積黍十二，羣情共知；

translations.literal: Considering Chong forged the inch with twelve millet accumulated—all knew it in common;
translations.idiomatic: All knew Chong made the inch from twelve millet;

sentences.zh: 而芳造寸，唯止十黍，亦俱先朝詔書。

translations.literal: while Fang's inch used only ten millet—both likewise followed prior edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's inch used only ten—both cited prior edicts.

sentences.zh: 以黍成寸，首尾歷然，寧有輒欲自取之理？

translations.literal: Making the inch from millet, head and tail clear in the record—how could there be rash wish to take it for oneself?
translations.idiomatic: The millet-to-inch chain is explicit in the record—who could seize it for himself?

sentences.zh: 肇任居端右，百僚是望，言行動靜，必副具瞻。

translations.literal: Zhao's post stands at the right hand; the hundred officials look to him—word, act, movement, and stillness must match what all watch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stands at the minister's right hand; the hundred officials watch him—word and deed must match their gaze.

sentences.zh: 若恃權阿黨，詐託先詔，將指鹿化馬，徙日移天，即是魏之趙高，何以宰物。

translations.literal: If he relies on power to curry favor, fraudulently lodges on a prior edict, and would turn deer to horses or shift sun and move heaven, he is Zhao Gao of Wei—how can he govern things?
translations.idiomatic: If he curries power, fakes old edicts, and would turn deer to horses or move heaven, he is Wei's Zhao Gao—how can he govern?

sentences.zh: 肇若無此，匡既誣毀宰相，訕謗明時。

translations.literal: If Zhao has none of this, Kuang has slandered the chief minister and mocked the bright age.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao did none of this, Kuang has slandered the chief minister and mocked a bright age.

sentences.zh: 豈應談議之間，便有指鹿之事；

translations.literal: Should there be turning-deer affairs in the midst of debate;
translations.idiomatic: Should debate hold turning-deer affairs;

sentences.zh: 可否之際，輕生刖足之言。

translations.literal: at the moment of yes and no, light words of cutting off one's feet?
translations.idiomatic: at the moment of judgment, talk of cutting off one's feet?

sentences.zh: 趙高矯惑，事屬衰秦；

translations.literal: Zhao Gao's false confusion belonged to declining Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao's fraud belonged to fallen Qin;

sentences.zh: 卞和抱璞，時遇暴楚。

translations.literal: Bian He embracing jade met violent Chu in its time.
translations.idiomatic: Bian He embracing jade met brutal Chu in its season.

sentences.zh: 何宜以濟濟之朝，而有斯謗者哉！

translations.literal: How should a court so teeming have such slander!
translations.idiomatic: Why should so teeming a court hear such slander!

sentences.zh: 阻惑朝聽，不敬至甚，請以肇、匡並禁尚書，推窮其原，付廷尉定罪。

translations.literal: Blocking and confusing the court's hearing is insubordination in the extreme—please forbid both Zhao and Kuang from the Masters of Writing, push to the root, and hand to the Court Director for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: They block the court's ear—insubordination at its height—bar Zhao and Kuang from the Masters of Writing and send both to the Court Director for sentence.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 有司奏匡誣肇，處匡死刑。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Kuang had slandered Zhao and sentenced Kuang to death.
translations.idiomatic: The offices ruled Kuang had slandered Zhao and sought death.

sentences.zh: 世宗恕死，降為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Shizong remitted death and reduced him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong remitted death and made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 又兼宗正卿，出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also made concurrent Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and sent out as Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand Director of the Imperial Clan and sent out as Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 匡臨發，帝引見於東堂，勞勉之。

translations.literal: As Kuang was about to depart, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: As Kuang set out, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 匡猶以尺度金石之事，國之大經，前雖為南臺所彈，然猶許更議，若議之日，願聽臣暫赴。

translations.literal: Kuang still spoke of measure, feet, metal, and stone as the great warp of the state; though earlier the Southern Terrace had impeached him, he was still allowed further debate—if debate came, he wished permission to hurry to court for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang still called measure and bells the state's great warp; though the Southern Terrace had impeached him, he might debate again—if debate came, he asked leave to hurry to court.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「劉芳學高一時，深明典故，其所據者。

translations.literal: Shizong said: "Liu Fang's learning towers over a generation; he is deep and clear in ancient precedent—what he relies on."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "Liu Fang's learning towers over his age; he knows antiquity—what he relies on."

sentences.zh: 與先朝尺乃寸過一黍，何得復云先朝之意也？

translations.literal: With the prior dynasty's foot the inch exceeds by one millet—how can he again say it is the prior dynasty's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: His foot's inch exceeds the prior dynasty's by one millet—how can he call that the old intent?"

sentences.zh: [12]兗州既所執不經，後議之日，何待赴都也。」

translations.literal: [12] Yan Province is already what you grasp without warrant; when later debate comes, why wait to come to the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: [12] Yan is already beyond your warrant; when debate comes, why return to the capital?"

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，入為御史中尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he entered as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's opening he entered as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 匡嚴於彈糾，始奏于忠，次彈高聰等免官，靈太后並不許。

translations.literal: Kuang was severe in impeachment; he first memorialized against Yu Zhong, then impeached Gao Cong and others for removal—the Empress Dowager Ling permitted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang impeached fiercely—first Yu Zhong, then Gao Cong—the Empress Dowager permitted none.

sentences.zh: 以違其糾惡之心，又慮匡辭解，欲奬安之，進號安南將軍，後加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Because it went against her heart in punishing what she hated, and fearing Kuang would resign, she wished to reward and settle him—he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, later added General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: It crossed her will; fearing he would quit, she promoted him—first General Who Pacifies the South, then General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 匡屢請更權衡不已，於是詔曰：「謹權審度，自昔令典，定章革歷，往代良規。

translations.literal: Kuang repeatedly asked to remake weights and measures without end; thereupon an edict said: "Careful weight and examined measure are canon from of old; fixing chapters and changing calendars are good rules of past generations."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang would not stop asking to remake measure; an edict said, "Careful weight and examined measure are ancient canon; fixing chapters and changing calendars are old good rules."

sentences.zh: 匡宗室賢亮，留心既久，可令更集儒貴，以時驗決。

translations.literal: Kuang of the imperial clan is worthy and bright and has long kept his mind on this; he may gather Confucian worthies again and test and decide in season.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang of the clan is worthy and has long studied this; let him gather scholars and decide in season.

sentences.zh: 必務權衡得衷，令寸籥不舛。

translations.literal: He must make the scales of weight attain the center and let inch and pitch pipe not err."
translations.idiomatic: Let the scales hit true center and inch and pitch pipe never miss."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「故廣平殤王洛侯，體自恭宗，茂年薨殞，國除祀廢，不祀忽諸。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The former Prince Shang of Guangping, Luohou, sprang from Emperor Gongzong; he died young in his prime; the state was abolished and sacrifice cut off—suddenly he was not sacrificed."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Prince Shang Luohou sprang from Gongzong, died young, and left no heir—the line broke and sacrifice ceased."

sentences.zh: 匡親同若子，私繼歲久，[13]宜樹維城，永茲盤石，可特襲王爵，封東平郡王。

translations.literal: Kuang was close as a son in private succession for years [13]; he should plant the wall of the realm and forever be bedrock—he may specially inherit the princely title and be enfeoffed Prince of Dongping."
translations.idiomatic: Kuang stood to him as a son for years [13]; let him be bedrock of the realm—inherit specially as Prince of Dongping."

sentences.zh: 」匡所制尺度訖，請集朝士議定是非。

translations.literal: When Kuang's forged measure was finished, he asked to gather court gentlemen to debate and fix right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang's measure was done, he asked the court to judge right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 詔付門下、尚書、三府、九列議定以聞。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the Secretariat, Masters of Writing, Three Offices, and Nine Columns to debate and report.
translations.idiomatic: The edict sent it to Secretariat, Masters of Writing, Three Offices, and Nine Columns for debate.

sentences.zh: 太師、高陽王雍等議曰：「伏惟高祖創改權量已定，匡今新造，微有參差。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang and others debated: "We consider that Emperor Gaozu created and reformed weight and measure and it was fixed; Kuang's new forging has slight discrepancy."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang and others wrote, "Gaozu fixed weight and measure; Kuang's new foot diverges slightly."

sentences.zh: 且匡云所造尺度與漢志王莽權斛不殊。

translations.literal: Moreover Kuang says the measure he forged does not differ from the Han Monograph's Mang weight and bushel.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang says his foot matches the Han Monograph's Mang weight and bushel.

sentences.zh: 又晉中書監荀勗云，後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。

translations.literal: Also Jin Secretariat Supervisor Xun Xu said that from Later Han to Wei the foot was longer than antiquity by more than four parts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Xun Xu said that from Later Han to Wei the foot ran more than four parts longer than antiquity.

sentences.zh: 於是依周禮，積黍以起度量，惟古玉律及鍾，遂改正之。

translations.literal: Thereupon according to the Rites of Zhou they accumulated millet to raise measure, took only the ancient jade pitch pipes and bells, and thereupon corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhou Rites they raised measure from millet, took ancient jade pitch pipes and bells, and corrected them.

sentences.zh: 尋勗所造之尺與高祖所定，毫釐略同。

translations.literal: Searching out what Xu forged, the foot and what Emperor Gaozu fixed were in hairs and hairs nearly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's foot and Gaozu's foot differed only by hairs.

sentences.zh: 又侍中崔光得古象尺，于時亦準議令施用。

translations.literal: Also Attendant-in-Chief Cui Guang obtained the ancient elephant foot-rule; at the time it too was approved for debate and ordered enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, Attendant-in-Chief, also found the ancient elephant foot-rule; the court approved it for use.

sentences.zh: 仰惟孝文皇帝，德邁前王，睿明下燭，不刊之式，事難變改。

translations.literal: Looking up to Emperor Xiaowen the Filial and Cultured, his virtue passed prior kings, his keen brightness shone below—an unerased pattern, affairs hard to change.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen's virtue passed prior kings; his pattern is not to be lightly changed.

sentences.zh: 臣等參論，請停匡議，永遵先皇之制。

translations.literal: We your subjects jointly debate and ask to stop Kuang's deliberation and forever follow the prior emperor's system."
translations.idiomatic: We jointly ask to stop Kuang's debate and forever follow the prior emperor's system."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 匡每有奏請，尚書令、任城王澄時致執奪，匡剛隘，內遂不平。

translations.literal: Whenever Kuang had a memorial request, Director Prince Cheng of Ren City often seized and blocked it; Kuang was narrow inside and grew inwardly unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kuang memorialized, Director Prince Cheng of Rencheng blocked him; Kuang, narrow by nature, seethed inwardly.

sentences.zh: 先所造棺猶在僧寺，乃復修事，將與澄相攻。

translations.literal: The coffin he had first built still stood in a monk's temple; he again prepared the affair, intending to attack Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin he had built still stood in a temple; he prepared again to attack Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄頗知之。

translations.literal: Cheng knew it fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng knew it well enough.

sentences.zh: 後將赴省，與匡逢遇，騶卒相撾，朝野駭愕。

translations.literal: Later as he was going to the ministry he met Kuang; their outriders struck each other; court and market were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Going to the ministry he met Kuang; their escorts collided; court and market gaped.

sentences.zh: 澄因是奏匡罪狀三十餘條，廷尉處以死刑。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon memorialized more than thirty charges against Kuang; the Court Director sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng memorialized more than thirty crimes; the Court Director sentenced Kuang to death.

sentences.zh: 詔付八座議，特加原宥，削爵除官。

translations.literal: An edict handed the matter to the Eight Seats for deliberation, specially granting leniency, stripping rank and removing office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the case to the Eight Seats; Kuang was specially pardoned, stripped of his title, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 三公郎中辛雄奏理之。

translations.literal: Langzhong of the Three Ducal Offices Xin Xiong memorialized to settle the case.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhong Xin Xiong of the Three Ducal Offices submitted a memorial to adjudicate the matter.

sentences.zh: 後特除平州刺史，徙青州刺史，尋為關右都督，兼尚書行臺。

translations.literal: Later specially appointed Inspector of Ping Province, transferred to Inspector of Qing Province, soon made Commander-in-Chief of the Pass West, concurrent with the touring secretariat of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made inspector of Ping, then of Qing, and soon commander-in-chief of Pass West with a concurrent Masters of Writing field staff.

sentences.zh: 遇疾還京。

translations.literal: Encountering illness he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，卒，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he died; posthumous title: Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Xiaochang and was posthumously styled Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 後追復本爵，改封濟南王。

translations.literal: Later his original rank was posthumously restored and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Later his original title was restored posthumously and he was re-created prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 第四子獻，襲。

translations.literal: His fourth son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son, Xian, inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate, titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, enfeoffments were lowered by precedent.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷十九上 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」。

translations.literal: Wei shu juan 19a: in the tables of contents of various editions this scroll is noted "deficient."
translations.idiomatic: Every edition's table of contents marks Wei shu juan 19a as "lacunose."

sentences.zh: 百衲本、南本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校語云：「魏收書景穆十二王列傳卷上亡。

translations.literal: The Bai nang edition, Southern edition, Ji edition, and Bureau edition at this scroll's end have a Song editor's note saying: "Wei Shou's book, Biographies of the Twelve Princes of Jingmu, scroll upper—is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Bai nang, Southern, Ji, and Bureau editions end with a Song note: "Wei Shou's scroll of Jingmu Twelve Princes, upper volume, is lost.

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。

translations.literal: " The Palace edition's textual verification says: "Wei Shou's book is lost; later people supplemented it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Kaozheng adds: "Wei Shou's text is lost; later hands filled it in.

sentences.zh: 」按此傳以北史卷一七景穆十二王傳補，間有溢出字句，當出於高氏小史。

translations.literal: " Commentary: This biography was supplemented from Beishi juan 17, Biographies of the Twelve Princes of Jingmu; now and then there are superfluous words and sentences that must come from the Gaoshi xiaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: " Note: This life was patched from Beishi juan 17 (Jingmu Twelve Princes); stray phrases occasionally must come from Gaoshi xiaoshi.

sentences.zh: 世宗景明元年薨於青州刺史 諸本「元」作「六」，殿本作「元」。

translations.literal: The Shizong, first year of Jingming, died in office as Inspector of Qing Province. In various editions "yuan" (first) is written "liu" (six); the Palace edition has "yuan."
translations.idiomatic: "Died as Qing inspector in Shizong Jingming year 1": most editions read yuan (1) as liu (6); the Palace text has yuan.

sentences.zh: 北史卷一七百衲本此字缺，他本或作「六」。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 17: the Bai nang edition lacks this character; other editions sometimes have "six."
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 17: Bai nang lacks the character; other witnesses read "six."

sentences.zh: 按景明無六年，頤死於景明元年十一月，見卷八世宗紀，今從殿本。

translations.literal: Commentary: Jingming has no sixth year; Yi died in the eleventh month of Jingming year 1, as seen in juan 8, Annals of Shizong; now follow the Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Jingming had no year 6; Yi died eleventh month, Jingming 1 (juan 8, Shizong annals); the Palace reading is adopted.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文 墓誌集釋元悰墓誌

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Wen. Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Cong
translations.idiomatic: "Posthumous title Wen": Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Cong

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一００〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 100〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 100

sentences.zh: 云：「諡曰文靖。

translations.literal: It says: "Posthumous title: Wen Jing."
translations.idiomatic: reads: "Posthumous title Wen Jing."

sentences.zh: 」墓誌與傳諡號不同者甚多，也有誌載諡而傳缺，傳載而誌缺。

translations.literal: " Epitaph and biography posthumous titles differ in many cases; sometimes the epitaph records a title and the biography lacks it, sometimes the biography records one and the epitaph lacks it.
translations.idiomatic: " Epitaphs and lives often disagree on posthumous styles; sometimes the stele records a title the biography omits, sometimes the reverse.

sentences.zh: 有的是先後改諡，有的是原諡不美，子孫私改，有的是後來補諡，不獨誌、傳有異，誌與誌間亦常不合，很難判斷是非。

translations.literal: Some are changed posthumous titles before and after; some are original titles not handsome, privately altered by descendants; some are later supplemented titles—not only epitaph and biography differ, epitaphs with epitaphs also often disagree; it is very hard to judge right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Some reflect later renamings, some ugly originals privately softened by heirs, some belated supplements—not only stele against biography but stele against stele; right and wrong are hard to settle.

sentences.zh: 今後凡諡號異同有無均不出校記。

translations.literal: Henceforth whenever posthumous titles differ or are present or absent, all will not be noted in collation.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter posthumous variants will not be recorded in collation notes.

sentences.zh: 遷冀州刺史 自此句至下文「遷右光祿大夫」一段北史卷一七無。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inspector of Ji Province. From this sentence down to the passage below "transferred to Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia"—a paragraph absent from Beishi juan 17.
translations.idiomatic: "Made inspector of Ji": from here through "made Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia" Beishi juan 17 has no parallel.

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋元遙墓誌

translations.literal: Commentary: Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Yao
translations.idiomatic: Note: Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Yao

sentences.zh: 〈圖版一０六〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 106〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 106

sentences.zh: 說他景明時「出拜鎮軍將軍、冀州刺史，入除護軍，加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Says that in Jingming times he "went out invested as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Inspector of Ji Province, entered dismissed as Guardian of the Army, added as Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia."
translations.idiomatic: says that in Jingming he "went out as general stabilizing the army and Ji inspector, came in as guardian of the army with the added rank of right Bearer of the Bright Insignia."

sentences.zh: 延昌中，淮泗不靜，加征南大將軍、南征諸軍事」。

translations.literal: In Yanzhou times, Huai and Si were not quiet; added as General Who Pacifies the South and Commander of the Southern Campaign armies."
translations.idiomatic: In Yanzhou, with trouble on Huai and Si, he was further named general pacifying the south and commander of southern campaign armies."

sentences.zh: 則遙為冀州刺史，在元恪的景明年間；

translations.literal: Then Yao as Inspector of Ji Province was in Yuan Ke's Jingming years;
translations.idiomatic: So Yao's tenure as Ji inspector fell in Yuan Ke's Jingming era;

sentences.zh: 是由冀州刺史入為右光祿大夫、護軍，非如此傳所云以左光祿大夫，領護軍，出為冀州，更不在「肅宗初」。

translations.literal: He was from Inspector of Ji Province entering as Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia and Guardian of the Army—not as this biography says, with Left Bearer of the Bright Insignia, holding Guardian of the Army, going out as Ji Province; even less at "the beginning of Suzong."
translations.idiomatic: he entered from Ji as right Bearer of the Bright Insignia and guardian of the army—not, as this life has it, as left Bearer leading the guard and then going out to Ji, and certainly not at "the beginning of Suzong."

sentences.zh: 此段當是補此傳者採自高氏小史或他書，弄錯了時間，遂致先後倒置。

translations.literal: This paragraph was probably taken by whoever supplemented this biography from the Gaoshi xiaoshi or another book, mistaking the chronology, thereby inverting before and after.
translations.idiomatic: The interpolator likely lifted this block from Gaoshi xiaoshi or another source, botched the dates, and reversed the sequence.

sentences.zh: 下文又說「遷右光祿大夫」，實即前「左光祿大夫」的重出

translations.literal: Below it again says "transferred to Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia"—in fact a repetition of the earlier "Left Bearer of the Bright Insignia"
translations.idiomatic: The later line "transferred to Right Bearer of the Bright Insignia" merely repeats the earlier "Left Bearer of the Bright Insignia"

sentences.zh: 〈北史已誤「右」為「左」〉

translations.literal: 〈Beishi already errs in making "right" into "left"〉
translations.idiomatic: Beishi already corrupts you (right) to zuo (left)

sentences.zh: ，插入的痕跡甚顯。

translations.literal: , and the traces of insertion are very clear.
translations.idiomatic: —the seam of interpolation is obvious.

sentences.zh: 表求改名芝 按上云「遙弟恒」，則其人初名恒，後改芝。

translations.literal: Memorial requesting to change name to Zhi. Commentary: Above it says "Yao's younger brother Heng"; then this person's original name was Heng, later changed to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: "Memorial to rename Zhi": above calls him "Yao's younger brother Heng"—so his original name was Heng, later Zhi.

sentences.zh: 據卷八世宗紀正始三年八月見「元恒」，而卷九肅宗紀孝昌二年六月丙子、孝昌三年正月甲申，卷一０孝莊紀武泰元年四月己亥，卷五八楊椿傳並見「元恒芝」。

translations.literal: According to juan 8, Annals of Shizong, eighth month of Zhenshi year 3 one sees "Yuan Heng"; while juan 9, Annals of Suzong, sixth month bingzi of Xiaochang year 2, first month jiashen of Xiaochang year 3, juan 10, Annals of Xiaozhuang, fourth month jihai of Wutai year 1, and juan 58, Biography of Yang Chun—all see "Yuan Heng Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong annals, juan 8, Zhenshi 3.8, cite Yuan Heng; Suzong annals (juan 9), Xiaochang 2.6 bingzi and 3.1 jiashen, Xiaozhuang annals (juan 10) Wutai 1.4 jihai, and Yang Chun's biography (juan 58) cite Yuan Heng Zhi.

sentences.zh: 疑初名「恒」，後加「芝」字。

translations.literal: It is suspected the original name was "Heng," later adding the character "Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: He probably began as Heng and later added the character Zhi.

sentences.zh: 汝陰王天賜和平三年封 按天賜於和平二年七月戊寅，與小新成、萬壽同日封，見卷五高宗紀，這裏「三」當是「二」之訛。

translations.literal: Prince of Runan Tiansi enfeoffed in third year of Heping. Commentary: Tiansi on day wuyin, seventh month of Heping year 2, together with Xiaoxincheng and Wanshou received enfeoffment on the same day, as seen in juan 5, Annals of Gaozong; here "three" should be the corruption of "two."
translations.idiomatic: "Prince of Runan Tiansi enfeoffed Heping 3": juan 5 (Gaozong) has wuyin day, seventh month, Heping 2, when he was enfeoffed with Xiaoxincheng and Wanshou—here "3" corrupts "2."

sentences.zh: 下樂浪王萬壽傳同訛。

translations.literal: Below, the biography of Prince of Yuele Wanshou has the same error.
translations.idiomatic: The life of Prince Wanshou of Yuele below repeats the error.

sentences.zh: 高祖器之 諸本「祖」作「宗」，北史卷一七作「孝文」。

translations.literal: Gaozu valued him. In various editions "zu" (ancestor) is written "zong" (ancestor/emperor); Beishi juan 17 has "Xiaowen."
translations.idiomatic: "Gaozu valued him": editions read zu as zong; Beishi juan 17 has Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 按元匡乃元濬

translations.literal: Commentary: Yuan Kuang is Yuan Jun's
translations.idiomatic: Note: Yuan Kuang was Yuan Jun's

sentences.zh: 〈高宗〉

translations.literal: 〈Gaozong〉
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong

sentences.zh: 弟新成子，若這裏作「高宗」，則下文元濬稱之為「叔父」，豈非顛倒？

translations.literal: younger brother Xincheng's son; if here it read "Gaozong," then below Yuan Jun calls him "paternal uncle"—would it not be inverted?
translations.idiomatic: younger brother Xincheng's son; calling him Gaozong here would make Yuan Jun's "paternal uncle" below nonsensical.

sentences.zh: 北史作「孝文」，補此傳者依魏書例，改作「高祖」，「祖」訛「宗」，今改正。

translations.literal: Beishi has "Xiaowen"; whoever supplemented this biography following Wei shu usage changed it to "Gaozu"; "zu" corrupted to "zong"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi reads Xiaowen; the patcher, following Wei shu style, wrote Gaozu; zu corrupted to zong—now restored.

sentences.zh: 而尚書令臣肇以芳造

translations.literal: And the Master of Writing Ling minister Zhao, on Fang's fabrication
translations.idiomatic: But Minister Ling Zhao of the Masters of Writing, on Fang's measure

translations.literal: 〈to〉
translations.idiomatic: to (lacunose)

sentences.zh: 仍云扶 按此段文義不可解。

translations.literal: still said Fu. Commentary: This paragraph's meaning cannot be understood.
translations.idiomatic: still said Fu. Note: This passage will not parse.

sentences.zh: 「造」下、「扶」下當有脫文。

translations.literal: Below "fabrication" and below "Fu" there must be missing text.
translations.idiomatic: Text is missing after zao (fabrication) and after Fu.

sentences.zh: 抑中無所 張森楷北史校勘記云：「疑『抑』是『折』之誤。

translations.literal: Yi in the center has nothing. Zhang Senkai's Beishi collation notes say: "It is suspected yi (restrain) is the error of zhe (break/fold)."
translations.idiomatic: "Yi in the center has nothing": Zhang Senkai's Beishi collation (suspected yi corrupts zhe).

sentences.zh: 」按通志卷八四下正作「折」，疑是。

translations.literal: " Commentary: Tongzhi juan 84 lower correctly has "zhe"; the suspicion is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Note: Tongzhi juan 84 lower reads zhe; the emendation is likely right.

sentences.zh: 恐此由心 張森楷云：「『此』疑當是『非』字，作『此』則與文義不相應。」

translations.literal: Fear this comes from the heart. Zhang Senkai says: "It is suspected ci (this) should be the character fei (not); written as ci it does not match the text's meaning."
translations.idiomatic: "Fear this comes from the heart": Zhang Senkai suspects ci (this) should be fei (not)—ci will not parse.

sentences.zh: 劉芳學高一時深明典故其所據者與先朝尺乃寸過一黍何得復云先朝之意也 按前贊劉芳，後不應說他所據與「先朝尺」不合云云。

translations.literal: Liu Fang's learning was high for the age and deeply versed in classical precedent; what he relied on compared with the Former Dynasty's foot-rule—yet the inch exceeded by one millet—how could one again say it was the Former Dynasty's intent? Commentary: Above one praises Liu Fang; below one should not say what he relied on did not match the "Former Dynasty foot-rule" and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The passage praises Liu Fang's learning yet faults his standard against the "former-dynasty foot" while calling the inch one millet too long and still invoking court intent—after praising Fang, the censure of his measure against the "former-dynasty foot" is incoherent.

sentences.zh: 據上王顯彈文，說「芳造寸，唯止十黍」，則所謂「寸過一黍」，明非斥芳，恐是指元匡所造尺。

translations.literal: According to Wang Xian's impeachment memorial above, it says "Fang's fabricated inch stops at only ten millet"; then the so-called "inch exceeding by one millet" clearly is not denouncing Fang—probably it points to the foot-rule Yuan Kuang fabricated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian's memorial above says Fang's inch used exactly ten millet; "one millet too long" therefore targets Kuang's rule, not Fang's.

sentences.zh: 這裏「其所據者」下當有脫文。

translations.literal: Here below "what he relied on" there must be missing text.
translations.idiomatic: Text is missing after "what he relied on."

sentences.zh: 大概是說劉芳根據的是「先朝」所頒尺，而元匡所造則「寸過一黍」，故下文斥責元匡「所執不經」。

translations.literal: Probably it means Liu Fang relied on the foot-rule promulgated by the "Former Dynasty," while what Yuan Kuang fabricated had "the inch exceeding by one millet"; hence below denouncing Yuan Kuang "what he held was uncanonical."
translations.idiomatic: Likely Fang followed the court's former promulgated foot, whereas Kuang's inch ran one millet long—hence the later charge that Kuang's standard was uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 今於「其所據者」下句斷。

translations.literal: Now at "what he relied on" below, the sentence is broken off.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence is broken after "what he relied on."

sentences.zh: 私繼歲久 按上文明云元恪

translations.literal: Privately succeeding for many years. Commentary: Above the text clearly says Yuan Ke
translations.idiomatic: "Privately succeeding for many years": above Yuan Ke is named

sentences.zh: 〈世宗〉

translations.literal: 〈Shizong〉
translations.idiomatic: Shizong

sentences.zh: 時，匡已求紹洛侯封，經尚書議奏襲封，則並非私繼，且襲封已久。

translations.literal: at that time, Kuang had already requested to succeed the enfeoffment of Shaoluohou, passed through the Masters of Writing deliberation and memorialized to inherit the enfeoffment—then it was not at all private succession, and moreover inheritance of the enfeoffment had been long.
translations.idiomatic: when Kuang had already petitioned to inherit Shaoluohou, the Masters of Writing deliberated and memorialized the succession—hardly a private adoption, and long settled.

sentences.zh: 不知何以前後矛盾。

translations.literal: One does not know why before and after contradict.
translations.idiomatic: Why the account contradicts itself is unclear.
